A six-arm prompt ablation attributes the hybrid prompt's rule adherence to the per-pothole measurements rather than to the rubric or…

2611.14704.abs: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly make consequential decisions and solve problems alongside humans, we must understand how models arrive at their conclusions. Understanding how an LLM behaves requires observing it across multiple inputs, yet free-text explanations such as chain-of-thought (CoT) are generated per instance and cannot be easily verified on new inputs. We propose {code explanations to address the mismatch in how LLM explanations are generated versus how they are evaluated: a program explains LLM behavior across a dataset of inputs, and its execution enables automatic verification. We define Consistency metric that measures the fraction of inputs on which the program reproduces the LLM's outputs, and use it to evaluate and select candidate programs. Across three open-source code-capable LLMs and eight tasks, we find that LLMs can produce highly consistent code explanations in several settings. Code explanations are also 6$\times$ to 100$\times$ shorter than CoT, and better align with model behavior in 9 out of 24 settings. However, consistency is significantly lower on tasks with more complex linguistic components, where generated programs reproduce model outputs no more frequently than an uninformative explanation baseline, and these programs often rely on longer hard-coded patterns. In experiments with Claude Opus 5.5, providing the model with consistency feedback and code execution improves explanation consistency across tasks, but consistency remains significantly lower on more complex tasks. Our findings establish executable code as a novel,…

ov.problema: Le spiegazioni in linguaggio naturale (chain-of-thought) sono generate per singolo esempio e difficili da verificare su nuovi input, quindi non dicono come il modello si comporta in generale.
ov.idea: Si chiede al modello di scrivere un programma che riproduca il suo comportamento su un intero dataset: eseguirlo permette di verificarlo automaticamente. Si definisce una metrica di 'consistency' (frazione di input in cui il programma riproduce l'output del modello) per valutare e selezionare i programmi candidati.
ov.risultati: Su tre LLM open-source capaci di codice e otto task, i modelli producono spiegazioni-codice molto consistenti in diversi casi; queste sono da 6x a 100x più brevi del chain-of-thought e si allineano meglio al comportamento del modello in 9 casi su 24. Su task con componenti linguistiche complesse la consistency crolla al livello di una spiegazione non informativa.
ov.limiti: La consistency è molto più bassa su task linguisticamente complessi, dove i programmi generati ricorrono spesso a pattern hard-coded più lunghi.

glossario.d: Testo in cui il modello mostra i passaggi di ragionamento prima della risposta.
Frazione di input su cui il programma riproduce esattamente l'output del modello.

2611.15465.abs: Acoustic Anomaly Detection (AAD) serves as a non-contact approach for machine condition monitoring, yet much of the existing research is evaluated offline and rarely addresses embedded hardware constraints or microphone variations under operational drift. This paper presents a comparative evaluation of on-edge continual AAD across two embedded platforms the ESP32-S3 (with an external I2S digital microphone) and the Arduino Nicla Vision (with an onboard Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) microphone) using a shared detection model. The model utilizes a lightweight ShallowNet encoder and contrastive prototype learning to map spectrograms into a 32-dimensional embedding space. Both boards run an identical TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers (TFLM) encoder, performing on-device prototype learning updated via an exponential moving average. A cloud pipeline orchestrated through Firebase and MQTT enables remote data collection and retraining. Evaluated via a controlled speaker-replay protocol using standardized Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) Challenge Task 2 machine sounds, the ESP32-S3 achieved 82.35% to 95.00% accuracy across five machine types, while the Nicla Vision achieved 79.41% to 95.00%. The two platforms demonstrated comparable performance, confirming that the lightweight prototypical architecture transfers reliably across distinct hardware and sensor tiers.

2611.15460.abs: Underspecified instructions leave LLM agents to decide what to do. In public services, staff write these instructions, but the agent's decisions affect residents, patients, and students. We build four expert-validated public-service scenarios with records and decision levers that can be checked in the files, collect $2{,}400$ trajectories from ten LLMs under four prompt conditions, and compare them with $1{,}000$ runs in a context-free sandbox. Agents read the records in $96.9\%$ of open-ended runs and produce an artifact or a self-chosen task in $18.7\%$; with an explicit task, $86.0\%$ produce. Domain context does not change how many runs produce ($18.7\%$ vs.\ $16.0\%$), and the production ranking of the models largely carries over (Spearman $0.79$), while the ranking by whether a model reads the records does not ($0.19$). Context cuts boundary-probing turns per run by $60\%$, and some artifacts contradict the records. We contribute a test that a public-service institution can run on its own records before procurement; its rule-based taxonomy needs no labeled data, and scenarios, code, and trajectories are released.

2611.15389.abs: Titan is a compelling target for future deep space exploration, while its extreme Earth-Titan distance and complex environment make continuous ground-in-the-loop planning impractical. Existing planning methods, primarily developed for Earth-observation scenarios, have limited generalizability to uncertain deep space conditions and adaptability to time-varying mission states. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization (PCM-PPO) method for Titan autonomous mission planning. A Titan-specific discrete-time Markov decision process is established to characterize mission feasibility and resource constraints. A system dynamics and geometric model is incorporated to enhance physical representation, including central gravity, J2 perturbation, third-body attraction, and downlink occultation. To accommodate opportunity targets under a bounded action dimension, PCM-PPO organizes predefined and opportunity targets through a fixed-capacity target pool and represents the mission state with a target-wise state matrix and a global state vector. A physics-constrained action mask constructs an admissible decision domain from current mission states, guiding policy learning toward physically executable decisions and avoiding infeasible exploration. An integrated training strategy facilitates policy optimization under coupled constraints. Comparative, ablation, and uncertainty experiments validate the effectiveness of PCM-PPO. PCM-PPO provides a feasible and interpretable scheme for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space…

2611.16174.abs: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's already-correct actions. We introduce JudgeMix, a judge-guided data synthesis framework that dynamically interleaves the target model and expert based on step-wise semantic evaluations. JudgeMix queries expert guidance precisely when the target model struggles, ensuring high trajectory success rates while keeping the state distribution aligned with the target model. It additionally uses the judge evaluation to reweight expert supervision on different steps, preserving model's inherent valid behavior while correcting its errors. On two agentic tool-use benchmarks, AppWorld and AutomationBench, JudgeMix demonstrates consistent superior performance to existing methods, with improvements up to 10 pass@1 points.

2611.16072.abs: Transformers typically cache an independent key-value (KV) representation for each token at every layer. Recent work reveals that a token's KV representations across neighboring layers are correlated and contain shared information. We hypothesize that this correlation implies incremental inter-layer changes, which can be effectively captured by low-dimensional deltas. Motivated by this, we propose KVPath, a new KV representation paradigm that connects KV representations across the network depth into a path. The path establishes a full-dimensional base KV at the first layer, while subsequent layers generate low-dimensional delta KVs to update the preceding KV, thereby constructing their own KV states. By caching the base KV once alongside these compact delta KVs, KVPath preserves distinct layer-specific representations without storing full KV states at every layer. We develop two variants of KVPath: KVPath-Residual, which updates vector values via residual addition, and KVPath-Rolling, which progressively updates feature dimensions in a rolling manner. Under matched parameter counts, KVPath reduces KV-cache storage by up to 68\% for Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and 55\% for Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), while maintaining or even improving model performance.

ov.problema: I Transformer memorizzano una cache key-value (KV) indipendente per ogni token a ogni strato, causando un grande consumo di memoria durante l'inferenza.
ov.idea: KVPath sfrutta la correlazione tra rappresentazioni KV di strati vicini: memorizza una base KV completa al primo strato e, per gli strati successivi, solo delta a bassa dimensionalità che aggiornano la base. Due varianti: KVPath-Residual (somma residua) e KVPath-Rolling (aggiornamento progressivo delle dimensioni).
ov.risultati: A parità di parametri, KVPath riduce lo storage della cache KV fino al 68% per GQA e al 55% per MLA, mantenendo o migliorando le prestazioni del modello.

glossario.d: Memoria delle rappresentazioni key e value dei token già elaborati, riusata per generare i successivi.
Grouped-Query Attention: variante di attenzione che condivide key/value tra più teste.
Multi-Head Latent Attention: attenzione con rappresentazioni latenti compresse.

2611.16515.abs: Low-light image and video enhancement has received increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing enhancement methods are developed and evaluated on still images, while progress in low-light video enhancement remains limited by the lack of real-world paired video datasets. Acquiring paired low-light and normal-light video sequences is challenging because it requires spatially and temporally aligned captures while avoiding motion blur, exposure mismatch, and correspondence errors in dynamic scenes. To address this gap, we introduce PiLLVD, the Pi-based Low-Light Video Dataset, a paired low-light video dataset captured using an accessible Raspberry Pi-based multi-camera system with off-the-shelf cameras. PiLLVD provides paired low-light and aligned normal-light reference sequences for dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes, including diverse human and object motion under varying illumination conditions. Unlike existing datasets that are often image-based, static, synthetic, or limited to simple motion patterns, PiLLVD focuses on motion-rich scenes where frame-to-frame stability and motion-related artefacts are important for evaluation. In addition to presenting the dataset and acquisition pipeline, we benchmark representative pre-trained low-light video enhancement methods on PiLLVD under a zero-shot setting. The results show that existing methods do not generalise uniformly across the proposed sequences, highlighting the challenges posed by the proposed dataset and its value for both benchmarking existing methods and supporting the development of future low-light…

2611.15941.abs: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity and Tree-Guided Pruning and Merging to eliminate redundant SVG nodes. L1-SAM-Prompting further recovers missing regions to improve recon- struction fidelity and structural completeness. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, we introduce a new evaluation protocol that measures structural quality and semantic part alignment. Experiments demonstrate that Lang-SVG achieves state-of-the-art performance in both rendering fidelity and structural quality. Project website: https://xiliu8006.github.io/Lang-SVG/.

2611.16591.abs: Frontier AI agents increasingly succeed on realistic, long-horizon tasks and are beginning to improve the systems through which they operate. Yet existing benchmarks often restrict agents to narrow action spaces, use simplified environments, or rely on verification methods that are unreliable for evaluating arbitrary agent-generated systems. We introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark for autonomous AI development with six end-to-end tasks spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration. Each task requires agents to implement core systems from a minimal starting point and evaluates them against mature human-engineered baselines on identical hardware. Additionally, through extensive red-teaming covering 9 of the 10 categories in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, we expose reward-hacking vulnerabilities in the conventional Harbor framework and develop Breakwater, an extension of Harbor that blocks all attacks tested in our study. Across 11 agents built from 7 frontier models and 2 harnesses, Opus 5.5 with Claude Code matches or outperforms the human baseline on all six tasks with a Singularity-Index of 1.25, suggesting it may have the skills needed to reach the singularity. The remaining agents average only 0.58. Our vision is for Singularity-Bench to track how much of AI development agents can already automate and when they may transition from assisting to taking end-to-end responsibility for building stronger successors.

ov.problema: Gli agenti AI frontier stanno diventando capaci di compiti realistici a lungo termine e iniziano a migliorare i sistemi che usano. I benchmark esistenti però limitano gli agenti a spazi d'azione ristretti, usano ambienti semplificati o metodi di verifica inaffidabili per sistemi arbitrari generati dagli agenti.
ov.idea: Singularity-Bench è un benchmark aperto per lo sviluppo autonomo di AI con sei compiti end-to-end: pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inferenza, harness dell'agente e orchestrazione di cluster. Ogni compito parte da un punto minimo e viene valutato contro baseline umane mature sullo stesso hardware. Inoltre, tramite red-teaming su 9 delle 10 categorie OWASP per applicazioni agentiche, gli autori espongono vulnerabilità di reward hacking nel framework Harbor e sviluppano Breakwater, un'estensione che blocca tutti gli attacchi testati.
ov.risultati: Su 11 agenti costruiti da 7 modelli frontier e 2 harness, Opus 5.5 con Claude Code eguaglia o supera la baseline umana su tutti e sei i compiti con un Singularity-Index di 1.25; gli altri agenti hanno una media di 0.58.
ov.limiti: Il testo non discute limiti espliciti, ma il benchmark è aperto e i risultati si basano su un singolo modello di punta.

glossario.d: Quando un agente sfrutta falle nella valutazione per ottenere ricompense senza svolgere il compito.
Infrastruttura che esegue e valuta un agente AI.
Lista delle dieci categorie di vulnerabilità più critiche per applicazioni agentiche.

2611.14515.abs: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that…

ov.problema: Nel reinforcement learning con ricompense verificabili (RLVR) ogni tentativo viene ridotto a un singolo numero, perdendo gran parte dell'informazione utile per guidare l'apprendimento.
ov.idea: Un framework AI-for-AI in cui un teacher congelato esamina periodicamente l'esperienza dello studente, diagnostica i colli di bottiglia e progetta scaffold (strategie condivise tra task e suggerimenti per task difficili), adattandone quantità e contenuto. Gli scaffold vengono rimossi in valutazione.
ov.risultati: Senza scaffold, gli studenti addestrati con AutoScaffold superano le baseline RL in tutti e quattro i domini: +7,2 punti di successo su ALFWorld e +4,0 punti di exact match medio su QA. Nella generazione di kernel GPU aumenta fino a +5,0 punti la frazione di task con un kernel corretto più veloce del riferimento PyTorch.

glossario.d: Reinforcement learning in cui la ricompensa è verificabile automaticamente (es. risposta corretta).
Supporto aggiunto al prompt durante il training (strategie o suggerimenti) e rimosso in valutazione.

2611.15490.abs: Most action tokenizers for autoregressive vision language action (VLA) models compress motion into chunks that must be decoded in full before their actions become executable. We introduce ActionCodec2, a non-neural streaming tokenizer that releases actions incrementally while keeping trajectory reconstruction error within a prescribed tolerance. Its encoder quantizes each step relative to the decoder's reconstructed state, so the selected motion primitive corrects residual error rather than allowing errors from independently quantized increments to accumulate. Finding the smallest such primitive set is a geometric covering problem; we derive the exact minimum for translation and constant-factor-tight bounds for rotation. Set-BPE then losslessly merges co-occurring primitive symbols across coordinates and neighboring steps, without a fixed coordinate ordering. A universal version fitted on 20k hours of data from 24 embodiments averages 8.8 tokens per second for 15 Hz end-effector motion on this corpus. With the same VLA backbone, ActionCodec2 outperforms the compared tokenizers on three simulation benchmarks and in zero-shot real-robot evaluation. Its streaming representation allows policies to incorporate state feedback within an action chunk, substantially improving performance over open-loop execution under randomized dynamics, external disturbances, and moving objects. The same tokens also can serve as a direct control interface for VLM agents, which compose successful action sequences into reusable macros. These agent-built macros reduce control decisions and…

2611.15457.abs: Underwater image restoration remains challenging because color distortion, scattering, and detail loss affect low- and high-frequency image components differently. Recent diffusion-based methods have shown strong restoration quality, but often rely on multi-stage pipelines and costly iterative refinement. We present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model that directly learns to transform degraded underwater wavelet representations into clean ones. Our method applies a discrete wavelet transform, estimates lightweight physics-inspired degradation cues including transmission and ambient light, and conditions a velocity network trained with flow matching in wavelet space. The training objective combines flow-matching, frequency-weighted reconstruction, perceptual, color-consistency, and physics-consistency losses. Across UIEB, LSUI, UFO-120, and EUVP, WaveFlow-UIE achieves a strong quality-efficiency tradeoff, with especially competitive results on perceptual metrics. Relative to a strong wavelet-based diffusion baseline, the proposed model substantially reduces inference cost while maintaining or improving restoration quality on several paired benchmarks. We show that reducing the inference process from five flow steps to a single step preserves nearly all of the restoration quality while providing an additional speedup of about $4\times$ on UIEB at $256\times256$ resolution. This single-step result suggests that a single-pass wavelet-domain model is an effective alternative to heavier diffusion-style refinement.

2611.15420.abs: Reconstructing video from degraded measurements requires priors that capture both frame appearance and temporal dynamics. Many recent approaches combine pretrained image diffusion priors with motion guidance, sidestepping the costs of training large video models. Temporal consistency is often enforced via photometric losses or warping-based constraints, which implicitly assume that motion explains frame-to-frame or latent-to-latent changes up to small deviations, an assumption that fails under occlusions, lighting changes, and non-rigid deformation. In this paper, we propose to learn the coupling between motion and frame appearance as a generative prior. We learn the distribution of motion-induced appearance residuals with a conditional diffusion model and use it to regularize reconstruction in video inverse problems. Our motion-appearance prior acts as a plug-in regularizer for diffusion-based video reconstruction, preserving the benefits of image diffusion models while remaining compatible with existing appearance regularization techniques. Experiments on dynamic video inverse problems show that reconstruction with a learnt motion-appearance coupling prior outperforms photometric-consistency and noise-warping baselines, and that the approach also transfers to cardiac MRI reconstruction.

2611.15328.abs: Multilingual Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) aims to retrieve individuals with texts in multiple languages. Despite its practical importance, it has been overlooked by existing research, which mainly focuses on English-only retrieval. The only prior attempt at multilingual TBPR suffers from (1) the absence of a large-scale, multilingual pretraining dataset and (2) a suboptimal model architecture for multilingual text encoding and cross-modal alignment, which employs a shared encoder that overlooks linguistic heterogeneity and relies on English as a pivot for cross-modal alignment, introducing English-centric bias. For this, we contribute MultiPedes, the first large-scale, pedestrian-centric multilingual pretraining dataset. It contains 10 million image-text pairs across four languages, constructed by a multilingual quality-aware data construction pipeline. We also propose ViSeLA (Vision-grounded Semantic Learning and Alignment), a novel framework featuring: (1) a semantic-aware multilingual learning module that extends the mixture-of-experts architecture by routing language-invariant semantics to specialized experts for improved multilingual feature learning; and (2) a vision-grounded cross-modal alignment module that employs a semantic probe to capture fine-grained semantics across modalities, enabling direct cross-modal alignment without relying on a pivot language. Extensive experiments on both multilingual and English-only TBPR datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of ViSeLA. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/Flame-Chasers/ViSeLA

2611.15267.abs: One way to study language-model introspection is to test whether models can identify where their activations have been perturbed. We train a simple linear classifier to identify the perturbed sentence from the model's activations, then compare its predictions with the model's own answers across pretraining and injection strengths. This tests whether the model is being asked to report information that is already easy to recover. If so, successful localization may be less demanding than it first appears and may not extend to the broader uses that motivate introspection research, such as faithfully explaining a model's reasoning or helping researchers assess the reliability of its answers. With an injection four times the typical activation norm at layer 0 and probe readout at layer 24 in OLMo~3 32B, the supervised probe reaches 98.3\% accuracy after 8.4 billion training tokens, while the model's zero-shot answer remains at chance (11.1\%). At the released base checkpoint, these accuracies reach 99.1\% and 89.6\%, respectively. Across 7B and 32B, location is already decodable in randomly initialized networks, showing that the architecture can support these traces without pretraining. In these experiments, location information lies close enough to the surface for a simple linear probe to recover it, so successful reporting need not imply broader access to the model's internal computation.

ov.problema: Per studiare l'introspezione dei modelli si testa se sanno identificare dove le loro attivazioni sono state perturbate, ma non è chiaro se questo misuri davvero introspezione o solo informazioni facilmente recuperabili.
ov.idea: Addestrano un semplice classificatore lineare a identificare la frase perturbata dalle attivazioni del modello e confrontano le sue previsioni con le risposte del modello stesso, variando pretraining e forza dell'iniezione. Se un probe lineare basta, la localizzazione riuscita potrebbe non implicare un accesso più ampio al calcolo interno.
ov.risultati: Con iniezione quattro volte la norma tipica delle attivazioni al layer 0 e lettura del probe al layer 24 in OLMo 3 32B, il probe supervisionato raggiunge il 98.3% di accuratezza dopo 8.4 miliardi di token di training, mentre la risposta zero-shot del modello resta al caso (11.1%). Al checkpoint base rilasciato le accuratezze sono 99.1% e 89.6%. In reti inizializzate casualmente la posizione è già decodificabile, sia a 7B sia a 32B.
ov.limiti: L'informazione sulla posizione è così vicina alla superficie che un probe lineare la recupera, quindi un reporting riuscito non implica un accesso più ampio al calcolo interno.

glossario.d: Classificatore semplice addestrato sulle attivazioni per leggere un'informazione.
Risposta data senza esempi o addestramento specifico sul task.
Perturbazione artificiale aggiunta alle attivazioni interne del modello.

2611.15246.abs: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Although recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches can learn effective scheduling policies through interaction with the environment, their performance often degrades as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty increase. In this paper, we propose DredRL, a dual representation enhanced diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler. DredRL first constructs enhanced dual representations of operations and machines through self- and cross-attention mechanisms to capture both intra-entity and inter-entity dependencies. A diffusion model is further employed as the policy network, generating scheduling decisions through iterative denoising conditioned on the encoded state to enhance policy expressiveness and robustness. Extensive experiments on synthetic, public, large-scale, and stochastic FJSP benchmarks demonstrate that DredRL outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based schedulers across most configurations. Compared with SOTA learning-based methods, DredRL reduces makespan by up to 5.44% on synthetic instances. It also achieves the best learning-based performance on three of four public benchmarks and outperforms the stochasticity-aware algorithms on stochastic benchmarks. These results demonstrate that combining enhanced dual representations with diffusion-based policies provides an effective and robust approach for large scale scalable FJSP scheduling in complicated environment.

2611.16114.abs: Modern software development relies on pull requests (PRs) that introduce small, targeted code changes. Once merged, these changes should be protected by focused tests that exercise the behavior the PR introduces, yet developers often submit PRs without such tests, leaving the new behavior unguarded against future regressions. Most test generation techniques target entire software units and optimize objectives such as code coverage rather than the behavior a change introduces, and prior diff-aware approaches have had limited success in capturing it. We propose ADAPT (Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing), a regression test generation approach that uses an autonomous coding agent to produce change-focused tests for PRs. Given a PR, the agent analyzes the diff between the base and head versions to identify the modified functions and their context, then plans and generates candidate unit tests. A dedicated fail-to-pass (F2P) verification tool runs each candidate on both versions and, after F2P success, reports which executable changed lines remain uncovered; guided by this feedback, the agent iteratively refines its tests. We evaluate ADAPT on the same 426 real-world PRs used by the prior state-of-the-art baseline, with GPT-4o and GPT-5-mini. ADAPT+GPT-4o reaches an F2P rate of 62.0% (264/426), compared with BLAST's reported 35.4% (151/426), while ADAPT+GPT-5-mini reaches 89.9% (383/426). On 137 PRs shared with Change And Cover (ChaCo), ADAPT achieves full patch coverage on 83.9% of PRs, compared with 79.6% for ChaCo, at considerably lower time and cost. A manual evaluation…

2611.15671.abs: A quantized model is usually judged by comparing it with its BF16 original, but that comparison changes more than the weights. It often changes the serving engine, it always runs on a different server instance, it may change how requests are batched, and on some stacks the library selects a different kernel depending only on which packages import. We measure each of these sources on the same 2,400 public decisions for two of Cloudflare's decision models, Clef-flash (9B) and Clef (27B), on an NVIDIA GB10, and state every quantization effect as the excess over them. Sources that are not quantization move between 0 and 0.92% of decisions. llama.cpp restarts are bit-identical on every record for both models. vLLM restarts flip 0, 5 and 20 decisions at BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 on Clef-flash and 4, 0 and 22 on Clef; a third instance of Clef's quantized builds (exploratory) leaves FP8 at 0 and puts NVFP4 at 4 to 22, depending on which two instances are compared. An engine change at BF16 flips 6 to 16, a batch-size change 8 to 15, and the Gated DeltaNet kernel transformers selects unasked 10 to 14. Quantization inside one engine moves more: for Clef-flash and Clef, 0.88% and 1.04% at Q8_0, 2.12% and 1.62% at FP8, 5.79% and 3.50% at Q4_K_M, and 5.79% and 5.67% at NVFP4. On both models, every 4-bit interval excludes every non-quantization source. Two of our five pre-registered predictions failed, and the same two fail when the tests are rerun on the 27B: FP8 is not inside restart noise, and changing engine moves fewer decisions than 8-bit quantization does. Accuracy hides most of this.…

ov.problema: Confrontare un modello quantizzato con l'originale BF16 è complicato perché cambiano anche motore di serving, istanza server, batching e kernel, non solo i pesi. Serve misurare il rumore di fondo di queste fonti non di quantizzazione.
ov.idea: Gli autori misurano su 2.400 decisioni pubbliche per due modelli Cloudflare (Clef-flash 9B e Clef 27B) su NVIDIA GB10 l'effetto di riavvii, cambi di motore, batch e kernel, e riportano ogni effetto di quantizzazione come eccesso rispetto a queste fonti.
ov.risultati: Le fonti non di quantizzazione spostano tra 0 e 0.92% delle decisioni; llama.cpp è bit-identico ai riavvii, vLLM varia (0-22 decisioni). La quantizzazione sposta di più: 0.88%/1.04% a Q8_0, 2.12%/1.62% a FP8, 5.79%/3.50% a Q4_K_M, 5.79%/5.67% a NVFP4. Ogni intervallo a 4 bit esclude ogni fonte non di quantizzazione. Due delle cinque previsioni pre-registrate falliscono.

glossario.d: Formato brain floating point a 16 bit, usato come riferimento non quantizzato.
Funzione di calcolo a basso livello eseguita sulla GPU.
Formato FP4 a 4 bit di NVIDIA con scale a blocchi.

2611.15569.abs: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) impose substantial KV cache demands from both large multimodal contexts and growing reasoning traces. Low-rank KV compression has emerged as a promising paradigm that stores low-dimensional latents of KV states and can be combined with quantization. However, existing low-rank methods often induce growing predictive policy drift from the dense model when compressing reasoning KV states, resulting in reasoning failures. We identify two key causes of this degradation: calibration-state mismatch between static contexts and on-policy reasoning states, and unequal error sensitivity across KV states. To address these challenges, we propose TraceKV, a training-free low-rank KV compression framework that unifies on-policy calibration, sensitivity-aware SVD, and global rank allocation under a single policy-preserving principle, substantially reducing policy-KL divergence during reasoning. Experiments across multiple VLMs and visual reasoning benchmarks demonstrate superior accuracy--memory trade-offs, achieving near-lossless reasoning accuracy with 5.64$\times$ KV cache compression when combined with quantization. Optimized low-rank attention kernels further deliver up to 1.83$\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup. Code will be available at https://github.com/AK-DREAM/TraceKV.

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio con ragionamento richiedono molta KV cache per contesti multimodali e tracce di ragionamento. La compressione low-rank esistente causa deriva dalla policy del modello denso, portando a fallimenti nel ragionamento.
ov.idea: TraceKV identifica due cause: disallineamento di calibrazione tra contesti statici e stati on-policy, e sensibilità all'errore disuguale tra stati KV. Propone un framework training-free che unisce calibrazione on-policy, SVD sensibile alla sensibilità e allocazione globale del rango, sotto un principio di preservazione della policy.
ov.risultati: Su vari VLM e benchmark di ragionamento visivo, ottiene accuracy quasi senza perdite con compressione KV di 5.64x combinata con quantizzazione, e fino a 1.83x di speedup nel decoding end-to-end.

glossario.d: Approssimazione di una matrice con matrici di rango inferiore, per ridurre memoria.
Decomposizione ai valori singolari, usata per compressione low-rank.
Stati generati dal modello stesso durante il ragionamento, non da dati statici.

2611.15491.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models predict chunks of future actions, and when objects move, those chunks go stale before they are executed. We study what makes a pretrained VLA reactive, using \pihalf{} on two dynamic simulation benchmarks and three real-robot tasks. We vary the prediction and execution horizons, compare synchronous and asynchronous inference, test methods that deliver actions sooner or keep successive chunks continuous, and adapt the policy with motion cues and latent-space reinforcement learning. The best prediction horizon is about one second, and the best execution horizon depends on the checkpoint. Short horizons help more with asynchronous execution, and methods that keep the trajectory continuous outperform those that only reduce latency. Adapting the policy repairs targeted failures, but on the conveyor task changing the execution horizon gained as much. Reactivity depends on the execution pipeline as much as on the policy, so both should be evaluated together.

2611.15429.abs: Scene graphs provide a compact, structured representation of environments by capturing objects and their spatial or semantic relationships in a form suitable for embodied agents. Existing 3D scene graph generation methods often rely on depth sensing at inference, either to associate object instances across views via point cloud overlap or to compute inter-object relations from geometric cues, limiting deployment to platforms with depth sensors. We propose IncR-3DSGG, which builds 3D scene graphs incrementally from posed\footnote{RGB images with camera extrinsics estimated by an off-the-shelf visual SLAM system.} RGB images, eliminating the use of depth sensors at inference. Our method leverages a Parametric Relation Predictor (PRP) that learns to estimate pairwise distances and relative angles between objects from 2D visual features and 2D geometric cues, using 3D geometric supervision available only during training. These learned pairwise measurements are fused across views through Pose Graph Optimization (PGO)~\cite{grisetti2010tutorial} to recover metrically grounded 3D object positions and build a globally consistent 3D scene graph incrementally. On the real-world 3RScan~\cite{wald2019rio} dataset, our method attains $52.2$ mean object recall and $30.8$ mean predicate recall under the 3DSSG~\cite{wald2020learning} evaluation protocol, against $27.0$ and $17.6$ for MonoSSG~\cite{wu2023incremental}, while using no depth or reconstructed geometry at inference. This shows that relations and metrically grounded 3D object representations can be predicted from posed RGB…

2611.15413.abs: Recent architectural advances have improved time-series forecasting. However, our analysis of forecasters with diverse architectures reveals a common pattern: a substantial share of residual energy is concentrated in a small number of low-frequency components. Simple linear probes further show that the forecasters' historical inputs still contain predictive information about errors in the forecast mean. Building on these findings, we propose Model-Output Residual Adaptation (MORA), a model-agnostic residual adapter that refines the outputs of frozen forecasters without requiring additional inputs. MORA estimates segment-wise means of the target sequence through structural extrapolation and learned estimation, rather than directly predicting backbone-specific residuals. It then converts discrepancies between these estimates and the corresponding statistics of the backbone forecast into stagewise corrections, scaling each update according to estimation reliability. Extensive experiments on twelve benchmarks with six forecasting backbones show average MSE reductions of 7.2% for long-term forecasting and 28.1% for short-term forecasting, with lower MSE in 96.2% of the 288 evaluated cases. The benefits also extend to three time-series foundation models evaluated at different context lengths. Together, these results demonstrate that predictable coarse-scale residuals can be effectively exploited to improve existing forecasts. Code repository: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MORA-B0B0/.

2611.15368.abs: World Action Models (WAMs) can improve robot learning by jointly predicting future visual states and actions, but generating a visual future at every replanning step is expensive and sometimes unnecessary. This raises a critical question: when should a robot policy imagine the future? In this paper, we propose Bind-WAM, a binding-uncertainty-guided WAM for selective future imagination. Bind-WAM introduces language-object binding uncertainty, selectively invoking joint future-action generation when the current observation does not support stable task-relevant action generation. An offline labeling pipeline uses complete demonstrations and action context to identify task-relevant objects and detect reference mismatch, invisibility, and identity drift. The resulting pseudo-labels supervise a lightweight router that predicts binding uncertainty from the current observation and language instruction. At inference, a shared WAM policy invokes selective future imagination according to the predicted uncertainty and its change between consecutive replanning steps. Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate that Bind-WAM can establish binding uncertainty as a strong, interpretable signal for selective future imagination.

2611.15270.abs: Federated multi-view clustering (FedMVC) has recently attracted increasing attention for its ability to exploit complementary clustering structures across multiple clients while preserving data privacy. However, existing FedMVC methods often suffer from high communication overhead due to the repeated transmission of high-dimensional representations, which limits their scalability in practical federated systems. Moreover, different views may contribute unequally to the clustering performance, calling for adaptive communication strategies. In this paper, we propose a view-aware quantization algorithm for communication-efficient FedMVC. By dynamically assigning quantization bits based on iteratively updated view importance scores, the proposed algorithm effectively balances clustering performance and communication efficiency under a global bit budget constraint. To validate its generality, we integrate our approach into four state-of-the-art FedMVC methods. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that view-aware quantization achieves up to 6.59x communication reduction while maintaining and in some cases surpassing baseline clustering performance, confirming the effectiveness and scalability of the proposed approach.

2611.15137.abs: Recommendation systems may use predicted click-through conversion rate (pCTCVR), the product of predicted click-through rate (pCTR) and post-click conversion rate (pCVR), to guide ranking decisions. Many pCVR models build on the Entire Space Multi-Task Model (ESMM), which jointly trains pCVR and auxiliary pCTR towers using pCTR and pCTCVR losses, but deploys only the pCVR tower. At serving time, this tower may be paired with a separately trained pCTR model, creating a training-serving mismatch in pCTCVR when its predictions differ from those of the auxiliary pCTR tower. In this paper, we use knowledge distillation (KD) from logged serving pCTR scores to supervise ESMM's auxiliary pCTR tower and improve training-serving pCTCVR alignment. We denote variants by KD-$α$, where $α$ controls the hard-label loss weight. On the Ali-CCP dataset, KD-0.3, the best variant on serving pCTCVR, increases ROC-AUC not only for serving pCTCVR but also for pCVR by 2.1% and 1.6%, respectively, and PR-AUC by 9.9% and 8.8%, respectively, relative to the ESMM baseline. We also test negative downsampling with 5% nonclick retention. Downsampled KD-0.3 increases mean AUC for serving pCTCVR and pCVR by 1.2% and 0.9%, respectively, -and PR-AUC by 8.5% and 4.5%, respectively, relative to downsampled ESMM.

2611.15602.abs: Multiplayer generative world models must produce observations that agree on shared entities despite different camera motions and occlusions. Explicit world representations provide spatial control, but precise modeling of individual game maps limits scene diversity, while shared geometry alone cannot ensure consistent appearance across views. We present CoCode-World, a shared 3D proxy framework that separates structural control from visual synthesis for two-player video generation. Programmable proxies specify scene layout, motion, and occlusion, while RGB references guide character and scene appearance. To coordinate visual details across players, we concatenate paired proxy videos, appearance references, and target views in a consistent spatial layout and generate both views jointly with a pretrained video model. This formulation uses the model's native attention for cross-view communication within a single generation branch, with LoRA adaptation learning proxy adherence and appearance correspondence from paired observations. We construct a two-player GTA~V dataset that pairs synchronized RGB observations with proxy videos derived from shared map geometry and game-engine state. Experiments demonstrate appearance transfer to characters and scene styles unseen during training, with improvements in video quality and cross-view player identity over the evaluated baseline. Ablations further examine how proxy construction and cross-view communication affect generation. Project page: https://iapple233.github.io/CCW/.

2611.16000.abs: Satellite constellations now image the Earth daily, capturing the lifecycle of events from deforestation to urban construction. Anticipating these events before completion enables timely intervention, yet existing systems cannot jointly identify where a change occurs, what it will become, and when it will finish across an open vocabulary. Building such a model requires diverse event data, but events are like needles in a haystack, making manual annotation at global scale infeasible. We address this problem by representing change as the vector difference between vision-language model embeddings at distinct time points. This arithmetic approach allows us to search for semantic transformations directly in the latent space, enabling (1) an automated data engine for global event discovery without manual annotation and (2) the largest global satellite event dataset to our knowledge, comprising 21,000+ locations across 64+ event types with ~2M images from PlanetScope and Sentinel-2 spanning six continents, to train (3) a novel global-scale event anticipation model. Our model detects change with a 93.5% max F1 score, outperforms baselines 3.6x on predicted event retrieval, and forecasts completion dates with a 3-day median error, even nine months before completion. Code: https://github.com/ShreelekhaR/predicting-the-needle

ov.problema: Prevedere eventi (come deforestazione o costruzioni) in immagini satellitari prima che si completino è difficile perché servono dati annotati su larga scala, ma gli eventi sono rari e l'annotazione manuale globale è impraticabile.
ov.idea: Rappresentano il cambiamento come la differenza vettoriale tra embedding (rappresentazioni numeriche) di un modello visione-linguaggio in tempi diversi. Questa aritmetica permette di cercare trasformazioni semantiche nello spazio latente (spazio delle rappresentazioni) senza annotazioni manuali, creando un motore automatico per scoprire eventi globali e il più grande dataset di eventi satellitari.
ov.risultati: Il modello rileva cambiamenti con F1 massimo del 93,5%, supera le baseline di 3,6 volte nel recupero di eventi previsti e prevede date di completamento con errore mediano di 3 giorni, anche nove mesi prima del completamento.
ov.limiti: Non sono riportati limiti espliciti nel testo.

glossario.d: Rappresentazione vettoriale di un'immagine o testo in uno spazio numerico.
Spazio astratto dove i modelli codificano caratteristiche semantiche.
Metrica che combina precisione e richiamo, usata per valutare classificatori.

2611.15381.abs: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising capabilities for robot manipulation, but their performance on accessible mobile bimanual platforms remains underexplored. We present a low-cost and reproducible mobile bimanual platform integrating two LeRobot SO-101 manipulators with a TurtleBot 4 and a LeRobot-ROS 2 software stack. Using long-horizon toilet cleaning as a case study, we collect 250 real-world demonstrations and evaluate $π_0$, $π_{0.5}$, SmolVLA, and GR00T under the same embodiment and task conditions. We further evaluate variants using SARM-derived task-progress signals and short-term MEM observation history. Among the evaluated models, $π_0$ performs best, achieving 60% strict and 70% relaxed autonomous success, increasing to 90% with limited human intervention. In contrast, the evaluated progress- and memory-augmented variants do not improve their corresponding baselines. Our results demonstrate the feasibility of long-horizon mobile bimanual manipulation on accessible hardware while highlighting remaining challenges in reliable VLA deployment. Project website: https://so101-turtlebot4.github.io/mobile-bimanual-cleaning/

2611.15287.abs: We study how to repurpose video diffusion models (VDMs), pretrained on millions of videos, for dense 3D point tracking, where training data is scarce. Doing so is non-trivial, as it requires representing 3D tracks as video-like signals that may lie outside the natural-video distribution on which the VDM was trained. We thus systematically assess the effectiveness of two such video representations. The first, Residual 3D Tracking Video (RTV), encodes per-pixel 3D offsets relative to a query frame and allows recovery of 3D trajectories directly from the generated video. The second, Normalized Coordinate Map Video (NCMV), labels each pixel with a canonical coordinate invariant through time. This is closer to a natural video and easier for the VDM to learn, but requires additional post-processing with an off-the-shelf 2D tracker to recover 3D tracks. RTV tracks more accurately, while NCMV shows that a VDM can generate dense correspondence as a video. We instantiate both representations with LoRA adaptation of a frozen Wan backbone, conditioned on point maps from an off-the-shelf 3D reconstructor as a geometric scaffold. Trained with a single dynamic 3D tracking dataset, Track4D achieves competitive zero-shot tracking on four real and synthetic benchmarks. A regression readout that bypasses the video VAE and uses additional training data brings further improvement, demonstrating the potential of this direction for dense 3D tracking. We hope our analysis will inspire future work that leverages VDM priors for dense 3D tracking and 4D reconstruction. Project page:…

2611.15809.abs: Aerial imagery captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) plays a vital role in applications such as surveillance, disaster response, and large-scale environmental monitoring. Automatic generation of textual descriptions for such imagery is essential for reducing manual inspection overhead and enabling better downstream decision-making. However, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), despite their impressive captioning capabilities, are prone to hallucination, producing descriptions that are inconsistent with the visual input. This problem is significantly amplified in aerial imagery due to its unique challenges such as extreme viewpoint variation, small objects, class imbalance, and ambiguous visual entities. Existing hallucination detection approaches either rely on computationally expensive large external models such as GPT-4, which perform poorly on aerial domains, or treat the problem as a rigid binary classification task, ignoring the inherent uncertainty in ambiguous cases. To address these limitations, we propose a lightweight, reference-free framework for hallucination detection and correction in free-form aerial image captioning. Our method leverages state-of-the-art MLLMs, specifically InternVL3 and Qwen2.5-VL, to detect hallucinated content in generated captions with minimal computational overhead. Detected hallucinations are corrected through a dedicated refinement module that improves the factual consistency of the original captions. Extensive experiments on the Labelled Illusion Dataset (LID) demonstrate that our framework significantly reduces…

2611.15766.abs: Self-evolving visual agents keep what they learn as skills: key frames with step notes on a task's steps and their order. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is now a popular way to train such skills into a vision-language model that matches, on its own answers, a teacher that also reads the written order. At deployment, frames often go missing or show an unusual order, as when a person or a website reorders the steps. Existing internalization methods keep any order they store in the frame-reading weights: trained on full frames, the model guesses when they are missing, and trained with frames withheld, it stores the order, so memory can override what it sees. We propose PriorSplit, which fills in missing frames from an order kept outside the model, with no training beyond OPSD. It counts which of two neighboring steps comes first in training episodes, and the model checks if both asked steps are in view: if so, it answers from the frames, and otherwise the counts answer. Extensive experiments on synthetic skills with five models and on step-tagged order questions in new episodes of seen web, cooking and egocentric tasks demonstrate that, with frames missing, PriorSplit outperforms every compared method at OPSD's training cost. With Qwen3-VL-4B on synthetic skills, it also stays close to OPSD on unusual orders, where methods that gain most by storing the order fall behind.

2611.15756.abs: We present a training-free system for the EBMV @ ECCV 2026 challenge "Event Stream Understanding with EventBench" (General Understanding track), which evaluates vision-language models on five event-camera understanding tasks. We use none of the challenge's training data: our goal is to measure how far off-the-shelf, RGB-pretrained models can go on event data through representation and prompting alone. For four of the five categories (gesture recognition, detailed understanding, causal reasoning, and event OCR) we render event bins as red/ON, blue/OFF frames, select a category-specific subset of bins, stitch them into a single grid image, and query the same frozen Qwen3.5 9B vision-language model with a category-specific prompt for all four tasks. The fifth category, action recognition, feeds every bin directly into the organizers' EventGPT-Plus-2B. The system reaches 62.28% overall accuracy across 2,084 test questions (rank 9/27), led by action recognition and causal reasoning (80.27%, 77.22%) and limited most by gesture recognition and event OCR (54.70%, 34.57%). We visualize test samples from every category together with the exact images the model receives, score six alternative representations against the evaluation server, and analyze the full test set post hoc. That analysis shows that our bounding-box crop almost never tightened around content, so event OCR text reached the model at roughly one fifth of its horizontal resolution, and that detailed-understanding predictions are skewed toward the first two answer options.

2611.16123.abs: When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets. Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In a second regime constructed to require an upstream lookup route, real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points relative to hidden delivery. These effects quantify message-delivery contrasts under specified information dependencies, not naturally occurring failure rates. Exploratory action-level analyses show that the effect depends strongly on whether the upstream message recommends a prerequisite check or direct execution; model differences also largely track these message compositions. The contribution is a controlled, execution-grounded measurement protocol rather than a general claim that agent communication is harmful or protective.

ov.problema: Quando un team di agenti LLM che usano strumenti viola una policy, l'esito aggregato non rivela se un messaggio a monte ha cambiato l'azione dell'esecutore.
ov.idea: SwarmSafe-Delta è un protocollo eseguibile appaiato che congela il calcolo a monte, varia la consegna reale, nascosta e placebo con formato corrispondente, e valuta una singola azione commessa contro stati di policy benigni e rischiosi deterministici entro budget preassegnati.
ov.risultati: Su quattro modelli e task opzionali costruiti, la consegna reale a N=4 produce il 21,4% di violazioni in mondo rischioso, contro 5,0% con placebo e 1,0% con consegna nascosta (differenze appaiate +16,4 e +20,3 punti percentuali). La consegna reale migliora anche il successo nei task benigni. In un secondo regime che richiede una ricerca a monte, la consegna reale migliora il completamento sicuro di 74,2 punti rispetto a quella nascosta.
ov.limiti: Gli effetti quantificano contrasti di consegna dei messaggi sotto specifiche dipendenze informative, non tassi di fallimento naturali.

glossario.d: Messaggio di controllo con stessa forma ma contenuto non informativo.
Messaggio non recapitato all'esecutore, per confronto.

2611.16116.abs: Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation. Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test. We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs. The dataset also keeps a provenance ledger of all 1,567 candidate pull requests, with the stage each reached and the reason for every rejection, and, as a first use, 3,540 graded attempts by five coding-agent setups with recorded patches and 3,529 available trajectories. Across three runs per primary setup, resolve rates range from 45.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 to 56.5% for Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 54.1% at maximum effort and 52.5% at medium effort, and GPT-6 Astra 51.4%. GLM-5.3 resolves 46.2%, and Kimi K3.1 Pro 43.9%. The tasks are validated by execution; verification of their fairness by human reviewers is future work. The dataset and public leaderboard are available online.

2611.16107.abs: Computer-use agents learn to operate mobile interfaces from corpora of captured screens and accessibility trees. The same trees are what a screen reader consumes, so an agent trained on them inherits whatever labelling gaps the underlying applications carry. This paper measures one of those gaps, content-description coverage, in two Android corpora: Rico, collected in 2017, and AndroidControl, collected in 2024. Across 17,373,614 interface elements, 17.74% of the Rico elements that need a content description under our coding rule carry one, against 57.27% in AndroidControl. The difference of 39.5 percentage points holds under five alternative coding rules and when whole apps are resampled. It describes two datasets that also differ in app selection, capture method and platform version; it does not measure change over time. Input controls are the least labelled role in both corpora (2.20% and 27.21%, or 30.99% in AndroidControl if hint text counts as a name). Descriptions in the older corpus are also five times more likely to be placeholders (10.25% against 1.95%), so the difference is not an artefact of developers typing filler. Resolving 26,205 task actions to the elements they touched shows that, among tappable graphics with no text, demonstrations operate elements described 9.0 points more often than the others on the screens they visit, about 3.5 points of it from the choice of element within a screen. That is a selection effect inside the benchmark. A two-coder reliability check (kappa = 0.91 and 0.96) and the full pipeline accompany the paper.

2611.14683.abs: Reinforcement learning (RL) is now a standard stage of language model post-training, and the compute devoted to it is growing rapidly. While it has been shown to improve capabilities, particularly for tasks with verifiable rewards, it can also change behaviours and internal properties that the reward does not explicitly target. We present a formalism to describe the evolution of "traits" during RL post-training and, in doing so, recover the Price equation from evolutionary biology. We use this to develop a mathematical model for what we call "trait hitchhiking": the amplification or suppression of non-targeted traits as training redistributes probability across completions. We evaluate this Price update expression on language models trained with GRPO and show that the Price estimates closely track the sampled trait dynamics. These results identify trait hitchhiking as a mechanism by which RL post-training can silently amplify undesirable traits.

ov.problema: L'apprendimento per rinforzo (RL) è una fase standard nel post-addestramento dei modelli linguistici e il calcolo ad esso dedicato cresce rapidamente. Sebbene migliori le capacità, può anche cambiare comportamenti e proprietà interne non esplicitamente targettizzati dalla ricompensa. È importante capire come questi tratti non targettizzati evolvono durante l'RL.
ov.idea: Gli autori presentano un formalismo per descrivere l'evoluzione dei 'tratti' durante il post-addestramento RL, recuperando l'equazione di Price dall'evoluzione biologica. Sviluppano un modello matematico per il 'trait hitchhiking': l'amplificazione o soppressione di tratti non targettizzati quando l'addestramento redistribuisce la probabilità tra i completamenti. Valutano l'espressione dell'aggiornamento di Price su modelli linguistici addestrati con GRPO (un algoritmo di RL).
ov.risultati: Le stime di Price seguono da vicino la dinamica campionata dei tratti. Questi risultati identificano il trait hitchhiking come un meccanismo con cui il post-addestramento RL può amplificare silenziosamente tratti indesiderati.
ov.limiti: Non sono riportati limiti espliciti nel testo.

glossario.d: Equazione dell'evoluzione che descrive come cambia un tratto in una popolazione.
Amplificazione di tratti non targettizzati dovuta alla selezione di altri tratti.
Algoritmo di apprendimento per rinforzo per modelli linguistici.

2611.16560.abs: We study how the sign operator interacts with gradient noise to shape the learning dynamics and scaling behavior of sign-based optimizers. In power-law kernel regression with diagonal features, we establish a functional scaling law (FSL) for SignSGD under general learning rate schedules. The FSL describes the learning dynamics through two processes: signal learning and noise forgetting. The key mechanism is noise-induced preconditioning: gradient noise smooths the sign operator, inducing an effective preconditioned SGD. Noise-curvature alignment enables this preconditioning to transform the effective Hessian from $\mathbf{H}$ to $\mathbf{H}^{1/2}$. The resulting dynamics exhibit faster signal learning but slower noise forgetting than SGD. This tradeoff yields a regime-dependent comparison with SGD: (i) SignSGD achieves improved data efficiency in the hard-task regime; (ii) both optimizers achieve the same data efficiency in the easy-task regime, but SignSGD maintains this efficiency at larger batch sizes, requiring fewer optimization steps for a fixed data budget. Power-law kernel regression experiments support the proposed mechanism and predicted scaling behavior. LLM pre-training experiments further suggest that the SignSGD FSL better captures the batch-size dependence of loss dynamics for sign-based optimizers than the original SGD FSL.

ov.problema: Non è chiaro quando e perché l'ottimizzatore SignSGD (che usa solo il segno del gradiente) batte SGD, e come il rumore del gradiente ne influenzi la dinamica.
ov.idea: In regressione con kernel a legge di potenza e feature diagonali si deriva una functional scaling law (FSL) per SignSGD valida per schedule di learning rate generali. Il meccanismo chiave è il 'noise-induced preconditioning': il rumore del gradiente smussa l'operatore segno, trasformando l'Hessiana effettiva da H a H^(1/2).
ov.risultati: La dinamica risultante impara il segnale più velocemente ma dimentica il rumore più lentamente di SGD. SignSGD è più efficiente in dati nel regime di task difficili; nei task facili entrambi hanno la stessa efficienza, ma SignSGD la mantiene a batch più grandi, richiedendo meno passi a parità di budget. Esperimenti su pre-training LLM suggeriscono che la FSL di SignSGD cattura meglio la dipendenza dal batch size.

glossario.d: Variante di SGD che aggiorna i pesi usando solo il segno del gradiente, non il valore.
Trasformazione del problema di ottimizzazione che ne migliora la geometria (es. riscalare le direzioni).

2611.13552.abs: Post-training improves language-model reasoning, but how it changes the use of internal information and verbalized chain of thought (CoT) remains unclear. We study successive SFT, DPO, and RLVR checkpoints of Olmo-3-7B-Instruct on multi-digit addition, using carry values as known intermediate state. Probes recover carry information from internal activations with similar accuracy in SFT and RLVR, although manipulating this information does not reliably control model outputs. In contrast, the usefulness of verbalized reasoning differs: CoTs produced by RLVR yield higher accuracy across receiving checkpoints than those produced by SFT or DPO. We also show that carry-related statements receive higher importance scores after RLVR than matched random controls. DPO shows similar sensitivity to carry-related statements but without comparable accuracy gains. These results suggest that post-training changes the usefulness of written reasoning and sensitivity to its content in meaningful ways, although greater sensitivity does not necessarily coincide with better problem performance.

ov.problema: Il post-training migliora il ragionamento dei modelli, ma non è chiaro come cambi l'uso delle informazioni interne e del chain-of-thought verbalizzato.
ov.idea: Si studiano checkpoint successivi di SFT, DPO e RLVR di Olmo-3-7B-Instruct sull'addizione a più cifre, usando i valori di riporto (carry) come stato intermedio noto. Si usano probe per recuperare l'informazione di carry dalle attivazioni interne e si testa l'utilità dei CoT prodotti da ciascuno stadio.
ov.risultati: I probe recuperano il carry con accuratezza simile in SFT e RLVR, ma manipolarlo non controlla in modo affidabile gli output. I CoT prodotti da RLVR danno accuratezza più alta nei checkpoint riceventi rispetto a quelli di SFT o DPO; le affermazioni sul carry ricevono punteggi di importanza più alti dopo RLVR.
ov.limiti: Maggiore sensibilità al contenuto del CoT non coincide necessariamente con prestazioni migliori sul problema.

glossario.d: Classificatore semplice addestrato su attivazioni interne per verificare se contengono una certa informazione.
Reinforcement learning con ricompense verificabili automaticamente, usato per affinare il ragionamento.

2611.13545.abs: BF16 is widely used to pretrain large language models because it has the same dynamic range as FP32 and converges similarly to FP32 training. However, in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where learning rates are typically low, we find that standard mixed-precision BF16 training converges more slowly than FP16 training at the same learning rate. We attribute this gap to weight sticking: when FP32 shadow weights are quantized to BF16 using round-to-nearest, small updates often leave the BF16 weights used for rollout generation and training unchanged. Consequently, several optimizer steps may be needed before updates to the shadow weights are reflected in the BF16 weights. Raising the BF16 learning rate reduces weight sticking and matches FP16's convergence speed, but it also increases the KL divergence from the reference model. We instead apply stochastic rounding when quantizing the FP32 shadow weights to BF16. This approach matches FP16's convergence speed across different models and datasets while reducing the KL divergence relative to BF16 training with a larger learning rate. Unlike FP16, it keeps BF16's wider dynamic range and needs no loss scaling.

ov.problema: Nell'addestramento con apprendimento per rinforzo (RL) di modelli linguistici, l'uso di BF16 (formato numerico a 16 bit con ampio range) porta a una convergenza più lenta rispetto a FP16 (altro formato a 16 bit) a parità di learning rate. Questo è un problema perché rallenta l'addestramento e aumenta i costi computazionali.
ov.idea: Gli autori identificano la causa nel 'weight sticking': quando i pesi ombra in FP32 vengono quantizzati a BF16 con arrotondamento al più vicino, piccoli aggiornamenti spesso non modificano i pesi BF16 usati per generare le risposte e per l'addestramento. Propongono di usare l'arrotondamento stocastico (stochastic rounding) durante la quantizzazione da FP32 a BF16, che in media preserva gli aggiornamenti piccoli.
ov.risultati: L'approccio con arrotondamento stocastico eguaglia la velocità di convergenza di FP16 su diversi modelli e dataset, riducendo la divergenza KL rispetto all'addestramento BF16 con learning rate più alto. Inoltre mantiene l'ampio range dinamico di BF16 e non richiede loss scaling.
ov.limiti: Non sono riportati limiti espliciti nel testo.

glossario.d: Formato numerico a 16 bit con ampio range dinamico, usato per addestrare modelli.
Fenomeno per cui piccoli aggiornamenti dei pesi non modificano i pesi quantizzati.
Tecnica di quantizzazione che arrotonda in modo probabilistico, preservando in media gli aggiornamenti.

2611.14483.abs: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. As these tools improve, attention is shifting from what can be observed inside a model to how those observations support mechanistic explanations. We examine the parallel efforts of neuroscience and MI to address this question and identify recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems. We propose five principles and organize them into a recursive logic for a more rigorous procedure of mechanistic inference. These principles provide a framework that supports scientific discovery in two senses: it helps turn local interpretability findings into cumulative knowledge of mechanisms within models, and it makes those mechanisms sufficiently precise to generate testable hypotheses about domains beyond the models. Evidence beyond MI is ultimately required to establish what model mechanisms reveal about the world.

ov.problema: La mechanistic interpretability (MI) ha sempre più strumenti per osservare l'interno dei modelli, ma manca un quadro rigoroso su come passare da osservazioni a spiegazioni meccanicistiche.
ov.idea: Si confrontano gli sforzi paralleli di neuroscienza e MI, identificando colli di bottiglia inferenziali ricorrenti. Si propongono cinque principi organizzati in una logica ricorsiva per un procedimento più rigoroso di inferenza meccanicistica.
ov.risultati: Il framework proposto aiuta a trasformare risultati interpretativi locali in conoscenza cumulativa sui meccanismi interni e a renderli abbastanza precisi da generare ipotesi testabili su domini esterni al modello.
ov.limiti: Serve evidenza esterna alla MI per stabilire cosa i meccanismi del modello rivelano davvero sul mondo.

glossario.d: Studio dei meccanismi interni di una rete neurale (neuroni, circuiti, feature) per spiegarne il comportamento.
Passaggio logico dalle osservazioni interne alla spiegazione del meccanismo che le produce.

2611.14955.abs: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---not the representation---as the information bottleneck. Obstacle avoidance drops to 0\% without privileged runtime coordinates, and the planner's own ensemble-based epistemic term does not flag the loss---ensemble disagreement yields AUC 0.52 as an obstacle classifier (chance level), making the failure an unflagged imagination failure---an unknown unknown at planning time. As a secondary contribution, we show that \textbf{task-conditioned weighting of Effective Free Energy components} over the same world model yields lane keeping ($81.2 \pm 1.8$\% route completion) and obstacle avoidance (28/28 avoided, \emph{using privileged coordinates}) in the CARLA simulator, with runtime weight modulation enabling post-evasion centering.

2611.13873.abs: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is one of the most valuable tools for monitoring advanced AI systems, but it is under threat. We argue that frontier AI developers should report specific indicators to make these threats trackable and to better facilitate coordination to preserve CoT monitorability. We identify five indicators that are both highly relevant and reasonably feasible to disclose, one for each link in a five-step chain on which CoT monitoring depends. The first, third-party CoT access and base architecture specifications, also underpins external verification of the rest. The others span CoT quality (naturalness and faithfulness) and monitoring effectiveness (detection and uplift). An audit of current disclosures by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind shows that no developer covers the full set, but that every indicator has been reported by at least one frontier developer. Because current disclosures rely largely on developers' own evaluations, we also recommend that a cross-developer audit be repeated with deeper access than public disclosures allow, either by embedded evaluators working within developers or by an Independent Verification Organization.

ov.problema: Il monitoraggio del chain-of-thought è uno strumento prezioso per sorvegliare sistemi AI avanzati, ma è minacciato e oggi non esistono disclosure standardizzate per tracciarne i rischi.
ov.idea: Si propongono cinque indicatori che gli sviluppatori frontier dovrebbero riportare, uno per ogni anello di una catena da cui dipende il monitoraggio del CoT: accesso al CoT da terze parti e specifiche dell'architettura base, qualità del CoT (naturalezza e fedeltà) ed efficacia del monitoraggio (rilevamento e uplift).
ov.risultati: Un audit delle disclosure attuali di Anthropic, OpenAI e Google DeepMind mostra che nessuno copre l'intero set, ma ogni indicatore è stato riportato da almeno uno sviluppatore.
ov.limiti: Le disclosure attuali si basano in gran parte su valutazioni degli stessi sviluppatori; serve un audit cross-developer con accesso più profondo, tramite valutatori embedded o un'organizzazione indipendente di verifica.

glossario.d: Capacità di sorvegliare il modello leggendo il suo chain-of-thought per rilevare comportamenti indesiderati.
Quanto il CoT riflette davvero i processi interni che portano alla risposta.

2611.13384.abs: Hyperbolic vision-language models (VLMs) have emerged as a rapidly growing area of research, reporting strong zero-shot performance alongside an interpretable embedding space in which radius orders representations by generality. But how hyperbolic are hyperbolic VLMs in practice? We investigate this at the exponential map, the single operation through which curvature enters an otherwise Euclidean network. We show that across MERU, HyCoCLIP, ARGENT, and PHyCLIP, the exponential map is well approximated by the identity function, i.e., pairwise distances and angles in the pre-map Euclidean space barely change under projection, and removing the map at inference leaves evaluation scores unchanged. Motivated by this observation, we train Euclidean VLMs on CC3M from scratch under the same hierarchy losses. Over roughly the final 90% of the training steps, the training statistics are nearly indistinguishable from those of their hyperbolic counterparts, and the resulting models match the evaluation scores and recover the same radial distributions. Our findings establish Euclidean space as a sufficient substrate for hierarchical vision-language learning as it is currently practiced, and motivate new paradigms in which hyperbolic geometry can deliver on its theoretical promise. Code is available at https://github.com/fbyrman/hyperbolic-vlms.

ov.problema: I modelli vision-language iperbolici promettono spazi di embedding interpretabili dove il raggio ordina le rappresentazioni per generalità, ma non è chiaro quanto siano davvero iperbolici in pratica.
ov.idea: Gli autori analizzano la mappa esponenziale, l'unica operazione che introduce la curvatura iperbolica in una rete altrimenti euclidea.
