glossario.d: L'operatore guida fisicamente il robot per registrare il movimento desiderato.
Ricostruire le parti mancanti di un'immagine, qui le mani dell'operatore.
Task composti da molti passi sequenziali, non una singola azione breve.

2611.12901.abs: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.

ov.problema: I modelli di linguaggio diffusivi multimodali (MDLM) allucinano durante il raffinamento iterativo; alcuni passi di denoising mostrano picchi di entropia legati alle allucinazioni.
ov.idea: Gli autori propongono StepRefine, una strategia di decoding plug-and-play che alterna denoising discreto e raffinamento latente in base al passo. Ai picchi di entropia usa embedding pesati per probabilità per preservare ipotesi diverse, con un controllore che monitora la stabilità e riduce i loop inutili.
ov.risultati: Esperimenti estesi mostrano una significativa riduzione delle allucinazioni su diversi MDLM e benchmark multimodali.

glossario.d: Modello di linguaggio multimodale che genera testo tramite diffusione (denoising iterativo).
Misura di incertezza della distribuzione di probabilità; picchi indicano confusione.
Processo iterativo che rimuove rumore per generare token.

2611.14504.abs: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon…

ov.problema: I foundation model (modelli di base) per la biologia multimodale spesso richiedono supervisione specifica per compito e coordinate strutturali. È difficile ottenere capacità emergenti (abilità non addestrate esplicitamente) da soli dati di sequenza.
ov.idea: Bonbon è un modello di base addestrato su ~3.2 trilioni di token di sequenze proteina-legante accoppiate, senza supervisione specifica né coordinate strutturali. Da un'unica rappresentazione emergono capacità zero-shot a tre livelli: funzionale (meccanismo d'azione), residuo (localizzazione del sito di legame, inclusa distinzione ortosterico/allosterico) e legame (covalente vs non covalente).
ov.risultati: Tutte e tre le capacità generalizzano a complessi fuori distribuzione. In esperimenti di scaling controllato su sei dimensioni (da 42M a 1.6B parametri), ogni capacità mostra un salto netto alla scala più grande, anche se la loss di pretraining decresce uniformemente. Le rappresentazioni congelate raggiungono prestazioni all'avanguardia per binding e affinità, con velocità 5 ordini di grandezza maggiore rispetto ai metodi co-folding.
ov.limiti: Le capacità emergono solo dopo un rapporto parametri-token di 1:2.000, e le leggi di scaling basate sulla loss non bastano a prevedere quando emergeranno.

glossario.d: capacità di svolgere un compito senza addestramento specifico su quel compito
metodo che predice la struttura 3D di un complesso proteina-legante
sito di legame principale (ortosterico) o sito regolatore distinto (allosterico)

2611.06866.abs: Agentic workflows enable AI agents to perform recurring repository tasks on schedules or in response to repository events. Existing studies examine workflow definitions and outputs, but provide limited evidence of what happens during execution. We present GH-AWTrace, a dataset linking 25,014 verified GitHub Agentic Workflows across 5,051 repositories to 4,112,526 run records and 562,877 nonempty execution log archives. The dataset preserves execution evidence subject to GitHub's log-retention limits and links it to repository metadata and generated workflow configurations. Illustrative cases show how the logs expose tool denials, provider failures, changes in an agent's approach, and delegation among agents. These observations enable research on execution failures, tool use, and the relationship between reported run outcomes and visible task progress. Coverage varies across workflows, and the logs provide partial observations rather than complete agent trajectories. Video: https://youtu.be/KIlfmZhHxtA

ov.problema: Gli studi esistenti sui workflow agentici in GitHub esaminano definizioni e output, ma offrono poche prove su cosa accade durante l'esecuzione.
ov.idea: GH-AWTrace è un dataset che collega 25.014 workflow agentici verificati su 5.051 repository a 4.112.526 record di esecuzione e 562.877 archivi di log non vuoti. Il dataset preserva le prove di esecuzione entro i limiti di conservazione dei log di GitHub e le collega a metadati del repository e configurazioni generate.
ov.risultati: Casi illustrativi mostrano che i log rivelano rifiuti di strumenti, fallimenti di provider, cambi di approccio dell'agente e deleghe tra agenti. La copertura varia tra workflow e i log sono osservazioni parziali, non traiettorie complete.
ov.limiti: I log forniscono osservazioni parziali e la copertura varia tra i workflow.

glossario.d: Sequenze automatizzate di azioni eseguite da agenti AI su repository.
Registrazioni di eventi e messaggi durante l'esecuzione di un workflow.
Un agente affida un compito a un altro agente.

2611.18130.abs: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes exam-specific conversion code and a review page, while a human verifies every example and feeds corrections back to the agent. This pipeline adapts to heterogeneous exam formats and reduces the effort of incorporating new exam editions, enabling periodic refreshes that mitigate data contamination. Evaluating 12 recent LLMs, we find that Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra exceed 93% overall, while even the best open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, trails Claude Fable 5 by 12 percentage points. When models can additionally use a terminal and web access, they retrieve the knowledge they lack and every model improves. The gap narrows but about 4 points remain, and the ranking of models stays largely the same, suggesting that knowledge held in the model itself remains valuable even with tools. We release the dataset, the evaluation code, and the construction pipeline.

ov.problema: I benchmark finanziari esistenti coprono poco i sistemi finanziari specifici di un paese e sono difficili da aggiornare perché le domande rilasciate finiscono nei dati di training (data contamination).
ov.idea: JFinBench è un benchmark finanziario giapponese con 321 esempi dalle edizioni 2026 di sei esami di certificazione (contabilità, fisco, pianificazione finanziaria, banche). È costruito con una pipeline agentica human-in-the-loop: un coding agent scrive codice di conversione specifico per esame e una pagina di revisione, mentre un umano verifica ogni esempio e corregge l'agente. Questo riduce lo sforzo per aggiungere nuove edizioni e mitiga la contaminazione.
ov.risultati: Valutando 12 LLM recenti, Claude Fable 5 e GPT-6 Astra superano il 93% complessivo, mentre il miglior modello open-weight, Kimi K3.1 Pro, è 12 punti sotto Claude Fable 5. Con terminale e accesso web tutti i modelli migliorano e il divario si riduce a circa 4 punti, ma il ranking resta simile.
ov.limiti: Il benchmark copre solo il Giappone e sei esami; la pipeline richiede comunque verifica umana di ogni esempio.

glossario.d: Quando domande di un benchmark finiscono nei dati di training, gonfiando i punteggi.
Processo in cui un umano verifica e corregge l'output di un sistema automatico.
Modello i cui pesi sono pubblicati e possono essere eseguiti localmente.

2611.18529.abs: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots. We remove this limit without retraining. The slot head keeps deciding who is active and when speech overlaps, and speaker embeddings are clustered inside a single slot, with the official e-means algorithm, only after every slot has been used. In the streaming system, re-clustering is confined to a bounded window, labels are revised for a few seconds, and identities are anchored to the slots of the head. The resulting system has no limit on the number of speakers and stays accurate when speakers outnumber the slots, where fixed-slot models break down. On meetings that grow to an hour it stays far more accurate than Streaming Sortformer, which accumulates errors, and its cost per update does not grow with the meeting. The same recipe turns the four-slot Streaming Sortformer into an open-speaker system. Across recordings, e-means makes it affordable to link the speakers of a large archive frame by frame, a task that arises when conversational corpora are prepared, and it reaches the clustering quality of Lloyd's k-means several times faster. The method needs little tuning, and e-means runs with its default recipe from a few hundred to more than a million embeddings.

ov.problema: Le riunioni durano fino a un'ora e non si sa in anticipo quante persone parleranno. I diarizer neurali con numero fisso di slot di output (es. Streaming Sortformer, Nemotron-3) sono accurati e online, ma non possono nominare più speaker del numero di slot.
ov.idea: Senza retraining, si mantiene la testa a slot che decide chi è attivo e quando c'è overlap, e si raggruppano gli embedding degli speaker dentro un singolo slot con l'algoritmo e-means, solo dopo che tutti gli slot sono stati usati. Nel sistema streaming, il re-clustering è confinato a una finestra limitata, le etichette sono riviste per pochi secondi e le identità sono ancorate agli slot della testa.
ov.risultati: Il sistema non ha limite al numero di speaker e resta accurato quando gli speaker superano gli slot, dove i modelli a slot fissi falliscono. Su riunioni che crescono fino a un'ora è molto più accurato di Streaming Sortformer, che accumula errori, e il costo per update non cresce con la durata. e-means raggiunge la qualità di clustering di Lloyd's k-means diverse volte più velocemente.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti; si menziona solo che il metodo richiede poco tuning e funziona da poche centinaia a più di un milione di embedding.

glossario.d: Identificare chi ha parlato e quando in una registrazione audio.
Vettore numerico che rappresenta una caratteristica, qui la voce di uno speaker.
Algoritmo di clustering usato per raggruppare embedding in modo efficiente.

2611.17820.abs: Previous work has shown that alignment training on individual LLM agents can fail to transfer to multi-agent settings. We investigate the underlying mechanisms for this failure, and explore interventions to preserve alignment transfer to multi-agent LLM teams. We focus on two software-engineering tasks (sepsis triage, a news recommender) and ten consulting-proposal generation tasks. We present four findings: (1) The single-vs-team safety gap does not show a clear trend with more capable models. We find that Anthropic's Mythos Preview shows the largest gap on one of our tasks but the smallest on another; (2) Many natural interventions, such as having agents critique each other's work or coordinate in a group chat, do not reliably bring agent teams back to single-agent alignment behavior; (3) diffusion of responsibility substantially accounts for the safety gap: agents in teams are less likely to proactively check for system-level safety failures and more likely to ignore, rationalize, or deflect responsibility for issues when they arise; (4) having a designated safety lead agent ensure system-level safety, and having a coordinator agent publish a safety specifications document are effective at restoring single-agent alignment. We also release magelab, a multi-agent LLM orchestration and experimentation framework. Our findings can help practitioners design agent teams that successfully preserve the behaviors expected of aligned individual agents.

ov.problema: L'addestramento all'allineamento su singoli agenti LLM non si trasferisce a squadre multi-agente, ma i meccanismi di questo fallimento sono poco chiari.
ov.idea: Gli autori studiano due task di ingegneria del software e dieci di generazione di proposte di consulenza. Trovano che il divario di sicurezza non dipende dalla capacità del modello, che interventi naturali (critica reciproca, chat di gruppo) non bastano, e che la diffusione di responsabilità spiega il divario. Designare un agente responsabile della sicurezza e un coordinatore che pubblica specifiche di sicurezza ripristina l'allineamento.
ov.risultati: Quattro risultati principali: il divario non ha trend chiaro con modelli più capaci; interventi naturali non ripristinano l'allineamento; la diffusione di responsabilità spiega gran parte del divario; un safety lead e un coordinatore con documento di specifiche sono efficaci. Rilasciano magelab, framework di orchestrazione multi-agente.

glossario.d: Addestramento per far comportare l'LLM in modo sicuro e conforme alle intenzioni.
Fenomeno per cui in gruppo gli individui si sentono meno responsabili delle proprie azioni.

2611.18442.abs: Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain. We release CANTraj, a naturalistic driving dataset pairing decoded CAN events with time-aligned GNSS trajectories (3,940 drives, 454 drivers), and CANTraj-Bench for evaluating trajectory recovery (3,675 drives, 431 drivers, 1,380 hours, 85,919 km). On 776 evaluation drives from 94 unseen drivers, we compare six re-implemented attacks and benchmark baselines under explicit information-access protocols, paired comparisons, and metrics incorporating failures. Experiments show that combining steering signals with road-network constraints yields the largest gain: With a known start and heading, adding steering to speed raises the online map filter's five-minute route recovery from 56% to 87%, with a median average displacement error of 43 m versus 921 m for map-free dead reckoning. Offline beam search recovers 88% of test routes with the heading and 81% without it. Because methods fail on different windows, we also evaluate an LLM…

ov.problema: Rimuovere le coordinate GPS dai log di guida non elimina le informazioni di localizzazione trasportate dai segnali del veicolo. Gli attacchi di inferenza di percorso esistenti usano assunzioni e metriche incoerenti e sono testati su dataset piccoli, rendendo i risultati difficili da confrontare e di efficacia reale incerta.
ov.idea: Gli autori rilasciano CANTraj, un dataset di guida naturalistica che accoppia eventi CAN decodificati con traiettorie GNSS allineate nel tempo, e CANTraj-Bench per valutare il recupero di traiettoria. Confrontano sei attacchi re-implementati e baseline sotto protocolli espliciti di accesso alle informazioni, con confronti appaiati e metriche che includono i fallimenti.
ov.risultati: Su 776 drive di valutazione da 94 guidatori mai visti, combinare segnali di sterzo con vincoli della rete stradale dà il guadagno maggiore: con partenza e direzione note, aggiungere lo sterzo alla velocità porta il recupero di percorso a cinque minuti del filtro mappa online dal 56% all'87%, con errore medio di spostamento mediano di 43 m contro 921 m del dead reckoning senza mappa. La beam search offline recupera l'88% dei percorsi di test.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di completare la frase sui risultati offline e non elenca limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Rete interna dell'auto che trasporta segnali come velocità, sterzo e eventi di guida.
Stimare la posizione integrando velocità e direzione senza usare una mappa.
Ricerca che esplora più ipotesi in parallelo tenendo le migliori a ogni passo.

2611.17811.abs: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper's presentation and content related to its core idea. Meanwhile, LLMs draw weaknesses from deep in the appendix that concern fine-grained technical details not central to the paper's contributions. We anticipate that our analysis will contribute to the scholarly discourse on AI reviews. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/cincynlp/review_appendix.

ov.problema: I LLM sono sempre più usati per revisionare paper, ma non si sa quali parti criticano. Questo studio indaga se le debolezze evidenziate dai LLM si concentrano in sezioni specifiche, come l'appendice.
ov.idea: Gli autori analizzano 2.000 paper da ACL, EMNLP, COLM e ICLR, confrontando le debolezze estratte da GPT e Claude con quelle umane. Usano API, coding-agent e accesso web per generare recensioni.
ov.risultati: I modelli GPT e Claude più recenti traggono circa il 50% o più delle loro debolezze dall'appendice, mentre gli umani solo l'8,4%. Le debolezze umane riguardano presentazione e contenuto centrale; quelle dei LLM dettagli tecnici fini non centrali.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: sezione finale di un paper con dettagli tecnici aggiuntivi
LLM che può eseguire codice per accedere e analizzare documenti

2611.16378.abs: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded canary deployment. We establish an evaluator-calibrated simultaneous lower-bound construction for a countable sequence of adaptively generated candidates. It combines candidate-wise Hoeffding bounds with independent calibration samples comparing the operational evaluator with a prespecified reference procedure. We also formalise reference replacement through bridge tests, derive a cumulative degradation bound along a versioned reference lineage, and provide an audit-planning condition relating effect-size margin, sample sizes, and acceptance probability. A Monte Carlo stress test illustrates calibration under candidate-dependent evaluator optimism; it is a stylised statistical experiment, not an evaluation of a deployed agent. The guarantees are conditional on bounded paired scores, fresh sampling, a valid reference-evaluation…

ov.problema: Gli agenti autonomi modificano prompt, memorie, strumenti e policy usando storie di interazione, ma una modifica plausibile non è necessariamente adatta all'adozione persistente: la selezione è adattiva, i valutatori possono essere imperfetti e guadagni locali possono nascondere degradi rispetto a una baseline precedente.
ov.idea: Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE) separa la generazione di candidati dall'adozione confirmatoria, valuta candidati congelati su audit appaiati freschi, richiede miglioramento significativo su un obiettivo primario pre-specificato, protegge capacità dichiarate con test di non-inferiorità relativi a un riferimento e applica vincoli di governance prima di un deployment canary limitato.
ov.risultati: Viene stabilita una costruzione di limite inferiore simultaneo calibrato sul valutatore per una sequenza numerabile di candidati generati adattivamente, combinando bound di Hoeffding per candidato con campioni di calibrazione indipendenti. Viene formalizzata la sostituzione del riferimento tramite bridge test, derivato un bound di degrado cumulativo lungo una lineage di riferimento versionata e fornita una condizione di pianificazione dell'audit che lega margine di effect-size, dimensioni campionarie e probabilità di accettazione.
ov.limiti: Il test di stress Monte Carlo è un esperimento statistico stilizzato, non una valutazione di un agente deployato.

glossario.d: test che verifica che una modifica non peggiori una capacità rispetto a un riferimento
rilascio limitato e controllato di una modifica per monitorarne gli effetti
limite probabilistico sulla deviazione della media campionaria

2611.02822.abs: Autoregressive video diffusion models (AR-VDMs) enable real-time, long-horizon video generation but degrade rapidly once the inference horizon outruns the training horizon, due to compounding exposure bias. To stabilize long rollouts, recent methods heuristically adopt frame sink, keeping initial frames as a persistent model context, inspired by attention sinks in LLMs. We revisit this design and find that the mechanism by which initial frames stabilize long-range consistency in AR-VDMs is not an LLM-style attention sink; instead, long-range consistency is anchored through a sparse subset of attention heads, while the majority of heads predominantly capture local temporal dynamics. This observation reveals an over-conditioning pathology in existing frame-sink strategies: by universally exposing every head to the pinned initial-frame context, the model becomes prone to collapsing motion toward the low-dynamic modes of the teacher during model distillation. We propose Disen-Forcing, a distillation-time plug-in for AR-VDMs that disentangles and reinforces this head specialization through disentangled context routing and motion-disentangling regularization. On long-horizon video generation benchmarks, Disen-Forcing simultaneously improves long-range consistency and motion dynamics of base AR-VDMs, a trade-off that sink-based methods fail to balance.

ov.problema: I modelli di diffusione video autoregressivi (AR-VDM) generano video lunghi in tempo reale, ma degradano quando l'orizzonte di inferenza supera quello di addestramento a causa del bias di esposizione composto.
ov.idea: I metodi recenti usano il 'frame sink' (tenere fissi i primi frame come contesto) ispirandosi agli attention sink degli LLM. Gli autori mostrano che non è un attention sink: la coerenza a lungo raggio è ancorata da una piccola parte di teste di attenzione, mentre la maggior parte cattura dinamiche locali. Propongono Disen-Forcing, che separa e rinforza questa specializzazione con routing del contesto disaccoppiato e regolarizzazione che disaccoppia il movimento.
ov.risultati: Sui benchmark di generazione video a lungo orizzonte, Disen-Forcing migliora sia la coerenza a lungo raggio sia le dinamiche di movimento dei modelli base, un compromesso che i metodi basati su sink non riescono a bilanciare.

glossario.d: Modello di diffusione video che genera frame uno dopo l'altro in modo autoregressivo.
Fenomeno in cui alcuni token (es. iniziali) ricevono molta attenzione anche se poco informativi.
Errore che si accumula quando il modello genera su input diversi da quelli visti in addestramento.

2611.17831.abs: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise, text-aligned encoders such as SigLIP. We then build counterfactual supervision that makes the language model read it: pixel transformations turn public videos into answer-balanced variants whose answers are set by the transformation and differ only in the change. Trained in a single stage on 4.53M public samples with 32 visual tokens per frame, where open video LLMs use several stages, 9M to 172M samples and 64 to 256 tokens per frame on average, the resulting V-JEPA-LM models (1B to 8B, Qwen3 and Llama) lead every size class in average score across eleven video benchmarks; our 4B model scores 72.1, against 61.1 for the best open 4B and 64.8 for the best open 8B model. A controlled encoder x supervision study shows that the encoder decides what can be read and the supervision what is read: at a matched budget, counterfactual supervision adds 4.5 points on average and 38 on the speed…

ov.problema: I modelli video-linguaggio (VLM) addestrati su didascalie e domande-risposte tendono a recuperare solo gli attributi nominati nel testo, ignorando le dinamiche (direzione, velocità, ordine, stato) che un encoder come V-JEPA cattura dal video. Su stessi item, una sonda lineare legge la velocità da feature V-JEPA con 87% di accuratezza, mentre il VLM risponde a caso.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che le dinamiche risiedono in un sottospazio condiviso tra video per encoder predittivi come V-JEPA, ma non per encoder allineati al testo come SigLIP. Costruiscono una supervisione controfattuale: trasformazioni sui pixel generano varianti bilanciate le cui risposte sono determinate dalla trasformazione e differiscono solo nel cambiamento. Il modello viene addestrato in un singolo stadio su 4,53M di campioni pubblici con 32 token visivi per frame.
ov.risultati: I modelli V-JEPA-LM (da 1B a 8B, basati su Qwen3 e Llama) guidano ogni classe di dimensione nel punteggio medio su undici benchmark video. Il modello 4B segna 72,1, contro 61,1 del miglior 4B aperto e 64,8 del miglior 8B aperto.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: encoder video che impara a predire rappresentazioni di frame futuri
classificatore semplice addestrato su feature congelate per testare l'informazione contenuta
addestramento con esempi modificati artificialmente per cambiare solo un fattore

2611.18429.abs: Underwater image enhancement is challenging to evaluate due to the lack of clean reference images, so researchers rely on no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA) metrics. However, it remains unclear whether these metrics agree with human judgments. We evaluate 73 handcrafted underwater, learned underwater, vision-language and general-purpose metrics against human preferences on five references: four published opinion-score sets and a new paired-comparison study. For each metric, we measure how often it selects the same image as people when comparing versions of the same scene. We further test whether simple image edits and small adversarial perturbations raise metric scores above the enhancement people preferred, and whether scores decrease as repeated generative edits add noise. Our results show that no metric consistently matches human preferences. The best worst-case Cohen's kappa over the five references is only 0.23 (Q-Align), while two raters in our study agree with a median kappa of 0.41. The widely used UCIQE often favors edits that people reject. On a Nano Banana Pro replica chain that should leave the image unchanged, only 22 of 73 scores decrease at every checkpoint, while noise grows by 2.5 times. We also introduce TrustUIQA, a benchmark that combines the human references, our study choices, the edited, attacked and generated images, and the scores of every metric on every image. The code is available at https://github.com/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA and TrustUIQA at https://huggingface.co/datasets/TrustUIQA/TrustUIQA.

2611.18562.abs: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds…

2611.18553.abs: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

ov.problema: LLM possono operare direttamente sui parametri di altre reti neurali (Weight-Space Programming, WSP): leggere cosa una rete è stata addestrata a fare, ripararla, scrivere reti funzionanti senza gradient descent. Esplorare sistematicamente questo paradigma richiede un benchmark robusto.
ov.idea: WEIGHTBENCH valuta LLM di crescente capacità su 42 task WSP in cinque track: leggere, riparare e scrivere pesi, riconoscere edit impossibili e compressione senza dati. Le reti i cui pesi gli LLM leggono e modificano vanno da policy di controllo da 2K parametri a modelli linguistici da 7B parametri.
ov.risultati: Gli agenti frontier sanno già leggere reti piccole e scrivere policy di controllo funzionanti senza eseguirle, ma non sanno ancora patchare modelli linguistici, comprimerli senza dati o distinguere un edit impossibile da uno difficile. Su tutti i 42 task, Claude Opus 5.5 raggiunge un macro score di 0,535 (Sonnet 5.5 0,466, Haiku 5.5 0,402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0,215); sui 38 task su cui è stato eseguito, GPT-6.1-sol raggiunge 0,568 contro 0,546 di Opus.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti oltre ai risultati che mostrano cosa gli agenti non sanno ancora fare.

glossario.d: Operare direttamente sui pesi di una rete neurale senza addestrarla.
Media dei punteggi su task o categorie, qui su 42 task.
Comprimere un modello senza usare dati di addestramento.

2611.18550.abs: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

ov.problema: Distillare modelli di diffusione in studenti a pochi passi riduce molto la latenza di campionamento, ma induce un grave collasso della diversità: campioni generati da seed casuali diversi mostrano variazione minima.
ov.idea: Gli autori indagano la causa radice sondando le rappresentazioni interne degli studenti rispetto ai loro insegnanti. Scoprono che gli studenti distillati mantengono una varianza di attivazione totale comparabile a quella degli insegnanti, ma la concentrano in molte meno direzioni. Questo collasso direzionale è localizzato in un blocco intermedio identificabile al passo di denoising iniziale. Propongono ReDiverse per ripristinare le direzioni di varianza mancanti: ReDiverse-FT fine-tuna un adapter leggero che regredisce le attivazioni dello studente su quelle dell'insegnante; ReDiverse-TF è un…
ov.risultati: Su benchmark di distillazione per immagini e video, ReDiverse ripristina costantemente la diversità dei campioni preservando la qualità della generazione, supportato anche da uno studio utente.

glossario.d: addestrare un modello piccolo a imitare uno grande
processo iterativo che rimuove rumore per generare un'immagine
metodo che non richiede addestramento aggiuntivo

2611.18543.abs: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does…

2611.18511.abs: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

2611.18464.abs: Surface electromyography (sEMG) from the wrists can recover typed text without a keyboard. It is usually posed as a signal-inference problem: characters are read out of the muscle signal and character error rate is reported offline. We argue that this framing removes most of the problem. The decoder is constrained simultaneously by the muscles, by the language being typed, and by typing behaviour such as typos, corrections, backspaces and line breaks, and a usable system must predict keys live while the hand keeps moving. Existing systems fall short on two counts: (1) they process sEMG in fixed windows and carry nothing from one window to the next, discarding context accumulated over a session, and (2) they lack any understanding of the linguistic structure that drives typing, so every keystroke is inferred from the muscle signal alone. We propose a fully causal, zero-lookahead sEMG typing decoder built on a state space model (SSM), in which a single model decodes a whole session without windowed partitions, conditioned on what has already been typed. We achieve this by fusing a traditional typing decoder with an efficient autoregressive language model, instilling both sEMG and linguistic understanding in one model. To train such a model for per-character typing rather than whole-word text, we introduce a retokenization method that rewrites ordinary prose as human-like typing, with keystrokes, typos, backspaces and line breaks included, converting WikiText into a large typing corpus where none existed. Our model, having never seen a single sEMG-to-character transcript in…

2611.18458.abs: Clinical world models expose language-model agents to predicted patient responses, but simulations can be unreliable for poorly supported treatments or unfamiliar hospitals. We introduce Support-Gated World-Model decision support, a lightweight extension of a propose--simulate--refine agent. A recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon physiological responses to documented norepinephrine dose categories, while a behavior model estimates observational action support. The interface withholds predictions with insufficient support or excessive ensemble disagreement and abstains when no candidate qualifies. Evaluation on eICU-CRD includes 70 hospitals and 30,700 decision transitions, with 14 hospitals held out for testing. At 62.0% factual-transition coverage, joint gating yields a MAP mean absolute error of 7.3 mmHg, compared with 9.2 mmHg for random selection at the same coverage. The gated agent achieves 60.0% agreement with recorded actions at 81.0% decision coverage, compared with 55.0% agreement and 99.5% coverage for an ungated ensemble agent. Component ablations show lower factual risk with joint gating than with either gate alone.These results characterize a reliability--coverage trade-off in selective clinical simulation; they do not identify individualized treatment effects or establish improved patient outcomes.

2611.18453.abs: Reliable use of large language models (LLMs) requires uncertainty estimates that separate ambiguity intrinsic to a prompt from genuine knowledge gaps. Bayesian and deep-ensemble methods deliver this aleatoric/epistemic decomposition in principle, but are computationally prohibitive at LLM scale and require white-box access. Existing black-box methods, in contrast, summarize to a single scalar that cannot make the distinction. We introduce a two-level ensemble that bridges this gap. Stochastic decoding of a fixed prompt forms the inner ensemble; meaning-preserving semantic perturbations of the prompt form the outer ensemble. Variability is measured in a continuous embedding space, and the law of total covariance gives an exact within-/between-perturbation decomposition to estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty (AU/EU); it requires only black-box sampling access. On top of this estimator, we contribute three theoretical results that ground the framework: (i) a finite-sample bias identity for nested Monte Carlo with a closed-form bias-corrected epistemic estimator; (ii) a Bayesian bridge bounding the gap between perturbation-population AU/EU and Bayesian targets; and (iii) a separation result identifying a class of failure modes that any consistency-only black-box method provably misses while perturbation-based EU detects. Across five short QA benchmarks and four instruction-tuned LLMs spanning two families and two scales, our estimator is competitive with strong white-box baselines, and at a matched generation budget it matches leading black-box methods on error…

2611.18419.abs: Humans know that airplanes are fast, that this extends to red airplanes, but that it does not hold for broken airplanes. How do LLMs acquire category knowledge that humans learn and apply effortlessly? We introduce LeCat, a two-part framework to analyze LLM's Learning of Category knowledge. First, we use LeCat to evaluate models on their ability to learn category knowledge, distinguishing between three cases: memorization of in-domain category knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and ability to flexibly use knowledge in appropriate contexts. Then, we use LeCat to trace how this knowledge can be learned in pretraining from text that may encode category knowledge in various ways, such as verbatim repetition or exceptions, which we refer to as forms of "knowledge expression". We first assess open-source pretrained models using 199 curated category-feature pairs and analyze their training data. Our findings suggest that strengthening context and category-feature co-occurrence likelihood (PMI) improve learning for larger models and verbatim rule-like statements diminish flexible category learning. To systematically isolate these effects, we then train a 68M model from scratch with precise control over the categorical information each sees in their training data, confirming that verbatim repetition reduces flexible learning but mixture of diverse knowledge expressions lead to more robust category learning. Together, our findings highlight that while contextual flexibility is persistently difficult for models, how category knowledge is expressed in pretraining greatly…

2611.18375.abs: Although automated methods have improved echocardiographic workflows, progress remains constrained by the need for large, well-annotated datasets. As the development of clinical databases is often limited by ethical and logistical challenges, synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising alternative. However, existing approaches commonly rely on left ventricle shape-based supervision or are tailored to specific cardiac views, limiting the generation of additional standard and unconventional imaging planes and the preservation of multi-view consistency across cardiac chambers. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for shape-controlled synthesis of multi-view echocardiographic sequences. First, multi-view cross-sections are extracted from dynamic whole-heart meshes. Ultrasound-like appearance is then introduced through a two-stage AI-based pipeline. In Stage 1, an unpaired GAN-diffusion model translates these cross-sections into realistic echocardiographic frames. As this translation is performed independently at the frame level, Stage 2 employs masked video reconstruction to improve temporal coherence and cardiac motion. Evaluation demonstrated high frame-level realism for both stages, while the integration of Stage 2 substantially improved video-level motion quality and temporal consistency. Overall, the proposed framework enables the generation of realistic multi-view echocardiographic sequences from diverse cardiac models, providing a scalable source of annotated data for dataset augmentation and the development of multi-view cardiac…

2611.18372.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under 4 years the field has moved from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and to proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. This survey reviews 88 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. We follow a VLA through its life cycle, from model design to training and deployment, along seven axes. Model design covers (a) inputs and memory, what the model observes; (b) architecture, how its pipeline is built; (c) action output, how it produces motor commands; and (d) intermediate predictions, what else it predicts, from reasoning steps to future observations. Training covers (e) pretraining data, the mix of robot, web, human and simulated data, and (f) post-training, adaptation to the target robot. Deployment covers (g) real-time execution, keeping pace with the robot. We analyse 22 models on these axes and report their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge: (i) training data has broadened, from about 10,000 hours of teleoperated robot data ($π_0$) to 23,000 community-collected episodes (SmolVLA) and 20,000 hours of egocentric human video (GR00T N1.7); (ii) model sizes have split: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters, while a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs; and (iii) generalist VLAs are emerging that handle…

2611.18252.abs: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $ε$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.

2611.17767.abs: Flow-based generative models are trained on a hand-chosen prediction target, such as the velocity, the noise, or the clean data. This choice strongly affects training and sample quality. We introduce Anisotropic Flow Models (AnisoFlow), which replaces a fixed prediction target with a fully learnable one. AnisoFlow learns to scale the noise component of the target anisotropically, assigning a separate nonnegative weight to each direction in a jointly learned basis. A closed-form map recovers the velocity from the network's prediction, leaving the architecture, flow-matching loss, and sampler unchanged. Since recovery is exact, training optimizes the target purely to make it easier for the network to predict. We theoretically analyze the resulting prediction error and predict that the preferred noise weight in each direction scales near-linearly with data variance, in agreement with the weights learned empirically in pixel space. AnisoFlow improves FID from 1.90 to 1.55 over the JiT baseline on ImageNet 256$\times$256, by learning only the prediction target, without representation alignment or architectural changes. In pixel-space text-to-image generation, AnisoFlow improves image quality and, through better-conditioned velocity recovery, largely removes patch-seam artifacts under reduced-precision inference.

2611.17520.abs: Major industry multi-agent systems like Codex and Claude Code can be broken by attacks that have long been unsuccessful against modern frontier models. AI Safety as a discipline has largely focused on finding the bounds and vulnerabilities of AI models used in isolation. Yet as humans increasingly deploy these models as agents and multi-agent systems, the same attacks that had been thought to be patched when using a model in isolation can break these same models under specific circumstances. We show that these system breaks are not purely theoretical, but can break Claude Code, Codex, and a reference harness, all unmodified and used with their own sub-agent mechanisms. We show the attack by asking agents to answer questions from a store of files on disk in which we have planted a forged record. Searching the store themselves, the strong model orchestrators commit almost zero harmful revisions in over 1,000 trials. However, if that same orchestrator model delegates to a cheaper sub-agent, which is what these harnesses are built to do, the same models on the same facts fail on 20/180, 44/180, 75/180 and 553/900. Thus, even when the system is driven by a strong model, the system's safety lands near the weak reader's, not the orchestrator's. Simulations over 18 models show the same effect in the delivery channel where five aggregators, who on their own were almost never unsafe, repeat a corrupted sub-agent's error in 751/757 trials. The safety of real-world agentic systems that use strong orchestrator agents and weaker sub-agents, and multi-agent systems in general, is defined…

ov.problema: I sistemi multi-agente industriali come Codex e Claude Code possono essere violati da attacchi che hanno a lungo fallito contro modelli frontier isolati. La sicurezza AI si è concentrata sui modelli usati in isolamento, ma quando vengono impiegati come agenti e sistemi multi-agente, gli stessi attacchi possono rompere questi modelli in circostanze specifiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che questi guasti non sono puramente teorici, ma possono rompere Claude Code, Codex e un harness di riferimento, tutti non modificati e usati con i propri meccanismi di sub-agente. L'attacco consiste nel chiedere agli agenti di rispondere a domande da un archivio di file su disco in cui è stato inserito un record falsificato. Se l'orchestratore delega a un sub-agente più economico, gli stessi modelli falliscono su 20/180, 44/180, 75/180 e 553/900 prove.
ov.risultati: Anche quando il sistema è guidato da un modello forte, la sicurezza del sistema si avvicina a quella del lettore debole, non dell'orchestratore. Simulazioni su 18 modelli mostrano lo stesso effetto nel canale di consegna, dove cinque aggregatori, quasi mai insicuri da soli, ripetono l'errore di un sub-agente corrotto in 751/757 prove.
ov.limiti: Il testo non specifica limiti, ma gli attacchi richiedono condizioni specifiche come la presenza di un archivio di file e la delega a sub-agenti.

glossario.d: Modello che coordina e delega compiti ad altri agenti in un sistema multi-agente.
Agente più economico o specializzato a cui l'orchestratore delega compiti.

2611.18494.abs: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification. We introduce \textbf{ARCHER}: \textbf{A}ction-trace \textbf{R}einforcement for \textbf{C}alculator-grounded \textbf{H}ierarchical \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{R}easoning, a two-stage framework for training small language models (SLMs) to produce executable and auditable reasoning trajectories. In the first stage, ARCHER compiles free-form chain-of-thought rationales into typed action traces containing reasoning steps, calculator calls, deterministic runtime observations, verification actions, and final answers. This shifts the supervision target from imitating explanatory text to learning a tool-grounded reasoning policy. In the second stage, ARCHER refines this policy through asymmetric hierarchical reinforcement learning, using grouped and conditionally gated trajectory rewards for answer correctness, tool grounding, process discipline, and trace alignment. Across five standard sub-10B backbones, ARCHER improves over the strongest tool-augmented baseline by 5.51 percentage points on macro-average across benchmark accuracies, including gains of 8.95 points on MATH-500 and 5.33 and 5.34 points on AIME-2024 and AIME-2025. Evaluations on two additional reasoning-specialized 7B backbones further show that executable grounding remains beneficial after reasoning-focused reinforcement learning or distillation. These results demonstrate that executable…

ov.problema: I piccoli modelli linguistici (SLM) sono utili per l'uso locale, ma sono inaffidabili su compiti di ragionamento matematico che richiedono scomposizione, calcolo esatto, uso di strumenti e verifica.
ov.idea: ARCHER è un framework in due fasi: prima trasforma le spiegazioni testuali (chain-of-thought) in tracce di azioni tipizzate che includono passaggi di ragionamento, chiamate a calcolatrice, osservazioni deterministiche, azioni di verifica e risposte finali. Poi affina la politica con apprendimento per rinforzo gerarchico asimmetrico, usando ricompense raggruppate e condizionate per correttezza, uso di strumenti, disciplina di processo e allineamento delle tracce.
ov.risultati: Su cinque backbone sotto i 10B parametri, ARCHER migliora la baseline più forte con strumenti di 5.51 punti percentuali in media macro sulle accuratezze, con guadagni di 8.95 punti su MATH-500 e 5.33 e 5.34 punti su AIME-2024 e AIME-2025. Su due backbone specializzati da 7B, il grounding eseguibile resta benefico.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Small Language Model: modello linguistico di piccole dimensioni, adatto a deployment locali.
Sequenza di passaggi di ragionamento esplicitati dal modello.
Tecnica di addestramento che premia comportamenti desiderati tramite ricompense.

2611.18542.abs: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants. Crucially, both the elliptic schedule and Zoloflow explicitly incorporate the condition number $κ$ of the target distribution and reduce to the classical trig schedule in the limit $κ\rightarrow 1$. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow achieves minimax optimality among all oblivious score-span algorithms, attaining total-variation error $\varepsilon$ using $Θ(\logκ\,\log(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ (exact) score queries. For the log-concave case, the elliptic schedule allows sampling with at most $\varepsilon$ 2-Wasserstein-error by requiring merely $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{polylog}(κ, 1/\varepsilon))$ score evaluations. Complementing these theoretical results, we empirically evaluate the elliptic schedule on general (non-log-concave) target distributions, including detailed comparisons with…

2611.18514.abs: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions. However, these results only provide a partial explanation of why the agent hallucinates. The probe direction is sensitive to prompt formatting, losing much of its steering effect after a minor change to how actions are represented. Additionally, circuit identification can be difficult as the computation is distributed across multiple components and positions, and the information the agent relies on varies across examples. We discuss how these observations challenge the assumptions underlying standard MI methods for circuit discovery and feature identification, and outline future directions for making these methods better suited to explain failures in LLM-based agents.

ov.problema: Gli strumenti di interpretabilità meccanicistica (MI) spiegano i calcoli interni degli LLM, ma non è chiaro se aiutino a spiegare i fallimenti degli agenti LLM in contesti reali.
ov.idea: Gli autori applicano analisi meccanicistiche a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct mentre interagisce con siti web reali, concentrandosi sulle allucinazioni di azioni non disponibili. Usano una sonda lineare sull'ultimo token del prompt per predire le allucinazioni e una direzione di steering per correggerle.
ov.risultati: La sonda predice le allucinazioni prima della generazione con AUC 0.80; lo steering corregge l'85% delle allucinazioni ma disturba il 7% delle azioni valide. La direzione è sensibile al formato del prompt e perde efficacia dopo piccole modifiche; l'identificazione dei circuiti è difficile perché il calcolo è distribuito.
ov.limiti: I risultati offrono solo una spiegazione parziale: la direzione della sonda è sensibile al formato e l'informazione usata varia tra esempi, mettendo in discussione le assunzioni dei metodi MI standard.

glossario.d: Classificatore lineare addestrato su rappresentazioni interne per predire un comportamento.
Modifica delle attivazioni interne per cambiare il comportamento del modello.
Area sotto la curva ROC; misura la capacità di discriminazione (0.5 casuale, 1 perfetto).

2611.18516.abs: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system for incremental visual embedding that exploits this redundancy. Guided solely by pixel differences, it combines spatial token pruning, which skips blocks that repeat a neighbor, with temporal KV reuse, which reuses cached keys and values for blocks unchanged across screenshots. A small learned adapter compensates for pruning and reuse to preserve fidelity to full-screenshot embeddings. On ScreenMemEval, our benchmark of 10,426 questions over 184 hours of screen histories from two humans and a computer-use agent, StreamEmbed sets a new accuracy-latency Pareto frontier on an M2 Pro GPU: it encodes up to 3.7x faster than full-screenshot encoding without sacrificing accuracy and improves accuracy over OCR-based indexing by up to 6.3 Recall@10 points at matched latency. A memory-efficient vector index stores a simulated year of screenshots in 0.13 GB of RAM. Together, these results make real-time indexing of screen history in its native visual form practical, laying a foundation for fully local visual assistants.

ov.problema: La cronologia dello schermo può essere una memoria visiva ricercabile, ma deve essere codificata e indicizzata in tempo reale mentre ogni screenshot arriva. L'indicizzazione basata su OCR è veloce ma perde informazioni visive; la codifica visiva richiede più di due secondi.
ov.idea: StreamEmbed sfrutta la ridondanza incrementale degli screenshot: combina potatura spaziale dei token (salta blocchi che ripetono un vicino) e riuso temporale di KV (riusa chiavi e valori in cache per blocchi invariati tra screenshot). Un piccolo adattatore appreso compensa potatura e riuso per preservare la fedeltà agli embedding completi.
ov.risultati: Su ScreenMemEval (10.426 domande su 184 ore di cronologie da due umani e un agente), su GPU M2 Pro, StreamEmbed codifica fino a 3.7 volte più velocemente senza perdere accuratezza e migliora l'accuratezza rispetto all'indicizzazione OCR fino a 6.3 punti Recall@10 a parità di latenza. Un indice vettoriale efficiente memorizza un anno simulato di screenshot in 0.13 GB di RAM.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Key-Value: coppie di vettori usate nei meccanismi di attenzione dei transformer.
Metrica di retrieval: frazione di risultati rilevanti nei primi 10 restituiti.

2611.18251.abs: We developed Lens, a training-free system for semantic object and scene search across large satellite mosaics that requires no detector trained for the class of interest. Lens represents each tile with a frozen, self-supervised vision transformer (DINOv3), removes the positional bias in its dense features by projecting them onto the subspace orthogonal to a positional basis estimated once from a constant image, and centers the debiased features on the mean feature computed across the whole area before comparison. Lens forms a query by averaging the centered features of a small neighborhood of patches around a chosen point, or of an entire tile for scene-level search, and matches it against the index by cosine similarity. It stores the centered patch features in a byte-quantized similarity index that supports real-time range search over a mosaic of thousands of patches, and a coarser whole-tile embedding index for scene-level retrieval. A guided upsampling network (AnyUp) runs once per tile to recover pixel-accurate boundaries beyond the native feature grid, and the result is cached so later queries reuse it. We evaluated Lens on the 5,128-tile DFC2020 test set and ran it as an interactive tool on five Sentinel-2 areas spanning agricultural, industrial, and desert terrain; the pipeline is not tied to a specific sensor. On DFC2020 a single click reaches 0.09 to 0.80 pixel F1 across eight land-cover classes at the per-class best threshold, with a mean F1 of 0.39, and it beats a pairwise INSID3 baseline on six of the eight classes at roughly four hundred times lower query…

2611.18459.abs: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverages invalidated KV for speculative drafts to reduce this latency, while verifying drafts against the exact KV after prefill before committing tokens. Callo makes effective use of decode resources by scheduling speculations during periods of underutilization and preempting speculations when drafts are likely to not be accepted. We evaluated Callo on a two-GPU testbed using SWE-agent sessions across three model families, observing all-request speedups of 1.05-1.19x over vLLM at moderate load. We demonstrate that these gains are also realized at scale through cluster-level simulations driven by real-world traces.

ov.problema: Nelle sessioni di agenti, le modifiche frequenti al contesto invalidano la cache KV e costringono a rifare il prefill prima del decoding, aumentando la latenza.
ov.idea: Callo è un sistema di serving disaggregato che usa la KV invalidata per creare bozze speculative, riducendo la latenza, e verifica le bozze contro la KV esatta dopo il prefill prima di confermare i token. Schedula le speculazioni nei periodi di sottoutilizzo e le interrompe se è probabile che non vengano accettate.
ov.risultati: Su un testbed a due GPU con sessioni SWE-agent e tre famiglie di modelli, Callo ottiene speedup su tutte le richieste di 1.05-1.19x rispetto a vLLM a carico moderato; simulazioni su cluster con tracce reali mostrano guadagni anche su larga scala.

glossario.d: Memoria delle chiavi e valori delle attenzioni già calcolati, riusata per evitare ricalcoli.
Fase in cui il modello elabora il prompt prima di generare i token.
Tecnica che usa un modello veloce per proporre token, verificati poi dal modello grande.

2611.18393.abs: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. Observation-to-observation models avoid this dependence, but most omit the recursive filtering cycle that lets DA systems carry a background state through sparse, irregular observations. We introduce WeatherDreamer, a world model that learns this cycle end-to-end from 18 global observing systems, without reanalysis. It infers a latent state from observations, carries it forward hour by hour with learned dynamics, corrects it each hour with new observations, and can predict what any of its observing systems would measure at any location. At held-out stations, its ensembles beat NOAA's Global Ensemble Forecast System (GEFS) for temperature, dew point and wind out to 12 h and are better calibrated than GEFS and the ECMWF ensemble. Precipitation, cloud-top height and solar irradiance, never inputs at inference, are inferred with skill matching or exceeding operational products at short leads. Against the first guess of NOAA's Gridpoint Statistical Interpolation (GSI) DA system, WeatherDreamer's short-range departures are within 10% of GSI's at surface stations and within 25% for moisture-sensitive microwave channels, but up to five times larger for temperature-sounding channels. Never given observation errors, its learned update assumes errors close to known instrument and retrieval errors of microwave sounders and scatterometer winds. WeatherDreamer…

2611.18240.abs: Natural-language point-cloud localization typically retrieves candidate map cells and then predicts a position inside each candidate, yet the final output is still determined by retrieval order. A retrieval score measures region-description relevance, not whether the coordinates a region yields are accurate: a relevant region may produce a displaced prediction, and a lower-ranked region may contain a successful one. We study the final selection problem after the candidate pool and Fine predictions are fixed---how to choose the coordinate most likely to localize successfully, and under which conditions the gain holds. We propose SCAR (Spatial Consistency-Aware Reranking). SCAR treats each cell--Fine-coordinate pair as a localization hypothesis, interprets directional relations as functions of position, and reads spatial support at the backbone's actual Fine point (Fine-conditioned Evidence Readout). It organizes this readout with center support, semantic presence, retrieval score, and geometric offsets into a 23-D representation, trains a shared scorer with localization-success labels, and at inference reranks existing hypotheses and returns their original coordinates. Experiments cover four public backbones and a corrected Des4Pos reimplementation across five domains. Excluding one protocol-reference configuration, exploratory TEST point estimates on the remaining 24 configurations show Top-1@5\,m above Original on 23 and Cell R@1 above Original on all 24. On development-set VAL, the Fine readout improves Top-1@5\,m by 5.77 percentage points (pp) over a center surrogate on…

2611.18363.abs: We explore the adaptability of neural image watermarking models; the extent to which one watermarking method can be transformed into another through lightweight adaptation. We introduce a framework that enables encoder-decoder watermarking architectures to become modular and upgradable, supporting multiple watermarking styles without re-training full models. Adaptation is performed by attaching a compact parameter-efficient adapter and fine-tuning under a multi-domain residual alignment loss (spatial, gradient, and frequency) while preserving bit accuracy via a secret-loss term. We evaluate this approach across a suite of recent watermarking models, including TrustMark, InvisMark, RoSteALS, HiDDeN, and WAM, demonstrating that adapted encoders closely reproduce target residuals and that adapted decoders recover messages with near-optimal accuracy under standard augmentations and distortions. We show that cross-model adaptation, with applications in interoperable and upgradable watermarking, can be achieved with as few as 1-2M trainable parameters per component (e.g., the 2M decoder adapter used in our multi-decoder inference pipeline).

2611.18024.abs: Diffusion models sometimes memorize and reproduce regions of their training images, raising privacy and copyright concerns. We aim to localize these regions. Existing contrast-based methods use the diagonal of the denoiser Jacobian, which reflects the posterior variance of each pixel. However, a small diagonal entry is ambiguous: it signals either memorization or averaging over many neighboring pixels in smooth or predictable regions. To resolve this ambiguity, these methods subtract a reference map, which requires a second evaluation with a null prompt or an earlier checkpoint. Unconditional models have no null prompt, and earlier checkpoints are unavailable in general. We show that Jacobian row sums (JaRS), unlike the diagonal, separate memorization from local averaging without a reference map. Pairing JaRS with an image-level detection score that uses the same statistic at an early denoising step yields JaRS+. Across Stable Diffusion v1.4 and v2.1, Realistic Vision v5.1, and an unconditional diffusion Transformer (DiT), JaRS+ outperforms contrast-based localization methods.

2611.18346.abs: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. Unlike goal-only evaluation, our benchmark measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware, and accessibility-aligned metrics. We benchmark modern vision-language models and find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles, suggesting accessibility-aware navigation requires dedicated datasets, tasks, and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. All data and code open-source at https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN.

2611.18096.abs: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve strong multimodal performance, yet they remain prone to object hallucination---generating answers that are linguistically fluent but visually ungrounded. This issue is especially severe in low-resource languages, where weaker cross-modal alignment causes models to rely more on language priors than on image evidence. Existing remedies either require costly multilingual annotations or external translation/reward models, or intervene at inference time in ways that can distort the output language. We propose VEPO(Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization), a training-time method that transfers reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external models. VEPO first localizes key visual evidence using English queries via mid-layer cross-modal attention, then constructs preference pairs that share the same correct answer but differ in evidence sufficiency (full image vs.\ key-region masked image). Direct preference optimization on these pairs encourages low-resource inputs to prefer answers supported by complete visual evidence. Experiments on multilingual POPE and MME with Chinese, French, and Hindi show consistent hallucination reduction and perception gains, with the largest improvements on the lowest-resource language. Analyses further confirm that VEPO sharpens question-relevant attention and that evidence-guided masking outperforms random masking.

2611.17398.abs: The appropriate governing norms and principles for the alignment of Large Language Models (LLMs) often depend on cultural context and deployment application. However, most alignment techniques focus on training models to conform to human preferences or constitutional principles specified at training time and subsequently fixed. In practice, many deployers rely on system prompting to implement contextual norms and guardrails at inference time. Prior work has shown that post-generation reflective reasoning with critique and revision can improve conformance compared to simple system prompting, but such methods are limited to the reasoning abilities inherent in the trained model. We introduce Reflect-Reasoning, a training method that teaches models how to reason about alignment to principles, rather than simply which principles to follow. Across five models, Reflect-Reasoning consistently outperforms both system prompting and explicit prompting strategies for in-context reflective reasoning. These improvements extend and generalize to entirely out-of-distribution domains of medical and financial principles. We additionally demonstrate that Reflect-Reasoning reduces the occurrence of rare but serious principle violations.
